Review Text:
Amazing! I took tons of videos and photos. We went all in with the Grand Denali Tour with Glacier Landing, and it worth the extra money. I am not sure how many flight tours I will do in my life, paying the extra to maximize the experience was worth it to me.

I took dramamine for the flight and still got motion sickness but not too bad, so if you are prone to motion sickness I would for sure take something.

I dressed a little too warm for the flight (leggings, t-shirt, long sleeve, long jacket and beanie) but took the jacket and beanie off during the flight. It was actually warm on the glacier because the sun was out but the pilot told us it can get cold quick if a cloud blocks the sun so I was grateful I dressed warm, as you can always layer down. You are also only on the glacier for 15-20 minutes.

If you are doing the glacier landing, I highly recommend wearing the boots they give you for over your shoes as the snow can be pretty deep on the glacier- some people that just wore their waterproof shoes ended up with snow inside their shoes and had wet feet for the flight back.

Such an epic experience! We took my parents, who are in their early 70s and my mother is terrified of flying - she did great - she was pretty scared during the flight but now it's all she talks about, is so proud of herself, and is open to doing a flight tour again in the future.

Our pilot Luke made us all feel comfortable - definitely in good hands! Everyone we encountered that worked there were kind and professional - highly recommend.

Review Title: On top of the world, once-in-a-lifetime experience
Review Text:
Incredible experience! There's nothing else that can compare to seeing this landscape from the air. Truly awe inspiring. If you only do one thing when you visit Alaska- do this!!

Everyone gets a window seat, which I think is great, and our pilot Daniel explained a lot of interesting things about the geography, climbing history, and what we were seeing. He also did turns specifically to make sure that both sides of the plane had good views of things. All seats are good views! He also offered to take pictures for people once we landed at base camp. Everyone has a headset so it's easy to hear why the pilot is saying, and the cabin is heated (though it can still be chilly).

The flights and views are weather dependent, but the staff does its best to keep people informed of the weather conditions and their top priority is to keep everyone safe (Of course, they can't control the weather and sometimes have to cancel flights, but safety is #1). The weather can be tricky but the pilots and rest of the team are experienced. We had some clouds in the area and the pilot explained some of how he was deciding where to fly and why based on that.

There is a souvenir shop with sweatshirts and hats and stickers, and fantastic new restrooms with a water bottle station. Probably the best bathrooms in town!

Review Text:
We watched the weather and when the forecast showed clear weather for the next afternoon, we booked a flightseeing tour that included a glacier landing. They were almost completely booked and they will refund if the flight is cancelled due to weather so you may not want to wait to book.

The information shows that you shouldn't bring a backpack or purse on board. I think that's due to a lack of secure storage space. My sister and I were both able to take our purses which we wore with cross-body straps and were small enough to sit in our laps during the flight. Upon arrival we were told to get everything we intended to take on the flight then we were each weighed with our gear. Long pants and closed toed shoes are required for a glacier landing and you should also have a jacket, hat, gloves and sunglasses. After we were checked in and weighed, we were given boots that slipped on over our shoes. They are easy to put on with velcro straps and a clip. My sister was wearing ankle height waterproof hiking boots and she was allowed to just wear those but the boots they provided were comfortable. We put those on before we got on the plane.

The pilot was friendly and knowledgeable. Our trip actually left a little early since the pilot and all of us (6) were ready to go. We flew through the clouds and also had fantastic views throughout the flight. Don't forget your camera. If you are prone to motion sickness, you might want to take something beforehand. Our flight was a little bumpy and swoopy. Every person has their own window.

Landing on the glacier was mostly smooth and we got out and walked around for about 20 minutes. You can't explore too far for safety reasons, but you can see a lot while you're there. Our entire trip took the exact amount of time advertised and it was great. If the weather cooperates, this is something to do. I was scared before we left but got over that quickly and really enjoyed it.

Review Title: Incredible company, outstanding pilot, breathtaking experience!
Review Text:
My husband and I visited Alaska for my first time in early August. We knew we wanted to experience a fly over Denali National Park. After researching the various tour operators offering this service, it was a no brainer to book with Talkeetna Air Taxi. Not only were their Trip Advisor and Google reviews great, but what sold me was their policy to rebook or refund their tours. The other companies had a much more rigid refund policy. For those who have never traveled to Alaska, the weather changes daily and can be dramatic as well.

We originally booked the Mountain Explorer with a Glacier landing for the first tour time of the day. There are multiple tour times offered throughout the day, so if the visibility or weather cancels an earlier tour, it’s possible to book a later tour if there is availability. We left the rest of the day open in our planning just in case.

Unfortunately, the weather was not great on the day of our tour so they called us to tell us it was cancelled. The rest of the tour times were cancelled as well. But they offered to rebook us on the Mountain Explorer tour the next day without the glacier landing with a refund of the difference in pricing, so we rebooked it.

When we arrived for the 4pm tour time the next day, they actually booked us on the South Side Explorer with glacier landing and we still received a refund on the difference in price. We were happy because we did want to have a glacier landing and we didn’t even ask, it was automatically done!

Our pilot was Luke. He was fantastic! Super chill and greeted us wearing jeans and a t-shirt. I actually sat in the first passenger seat behind the cockpit and watched him fly the plane. It was fascinating. Each seat of the plane had a headset with volume knobs on each ear. Luke pointed out the names of the mountain formations as we soared around them. It was magical! Ruth glacier is huge and glorious in the air. Unfortunately, Denali was hiding in the clouds but the views of the other mountains was spectacular.

The glacier landing was smooth. We had plenty of time to walk on the glacier and take pictures. It was worth every penny to have had the opportunity to do so.

Since we sat in the same seats on our return, Luke made sure to fly back the opposite direction so we could see the views we missed on the way up. As we left the Denali mountain range, we could see views of the Talkeetna valley and various rivers which were breathtaking! Smooth landing back at the airport.

Talkeetna Air Taxi is the best company for a fly over to Denali Park, hands down!

Review Title: Outstanding Flight Viewing and Glacier Landing!!
Review Text:
This was an incredible experience! Last year we went to Alaska and when we were at Denali, we went on a helicopter and landed on a glacier. I couldn’t get out because of knee issues because the first step was 2-3 feet high. This year we took our grandson to Alaska (his choice) for his high school graduation gift. After reviewing several options, I chose the small airplane flight to land on a glacier this year - the “Southside Explorer with Glacier Landing” tour.
I talked to Kayla several times when I was deciding on the best Glacier Landing tour and she was very helpful and answered a lot of questions. She assured me that there were stairs and I could get off and back on the airplane at the glacier. She was absolutely right!! I was so excited to get on the glacier. The glacier we landed on this year was much different than the one the helicopter landed on last year. This was a beautiful glacier with lots of snow on it, instead of ice on the glacier we landed on last year for 10 minutes from the helicopter. This year we got to play in the snow for 20 minutes and take awesome pictures of the glacier and mountains all around us. The windows on the airplane were extra large so you could see so much and get great pictures too because there were a special plastic. Last year we just flew to the glacier and back and saw what we could. On the airplane this year, we flew through Denali Park around the mountains and glaciers on the way to the glacier landing and back. It was a beautiful scenic flight. The entire tour was about 1 hr 30 minutes.
Everyone was so helpful and nice - including Kayla and the others at the desk where you check in, the people that help you get your glacier boots, the lady that kept everyone in order while waiting for our airplane, the guy that filled up the planes, the pilots that also provide information during the flight, and everyone else that helped in any way was just super nice! They all did everything they could to make you comfortable and make it a great experience!
The other thing that said a lot about their business was their cancellation policy. They allow you to cancel at anytime, with a full refund, because they understand the “uncertainty of the issues facing us in the world today”. Our flight was cancelled for 8:30 am due to fog. The pilots made the call on whether they felt it was safe. They were able to reschedule us for 1:00 pm that afternoon. When we checked in for the 1:00 flight, they talked to the group scheduled for that time and told us that the pilots weren’t sure if we would be able to land on the glacier because of the fog and questionable flight conditions. They followed it up by telling us if we couldn’t land we would receive a partial refund. We didn’t even have to ask! It was clear that they were very thoughtful and considerate of the people that chose to fly with them. That meant a lot to me!!
I can highly recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi as a great choice for flight viewing Denali National Park and landing on a glacier! My husband agreed that this was much better than the helicopter tour the year before and our 18 year old grandson loved it!!

Review Title: Highlight of a 14 day trip to Alaska - and there were many highlights!
Review Text:
We cruised into Alaska, spent 7 more days driving around. This was our first stop and probably the family highlight because we had never done a flightseeing trip before.

Upon arrival, we were told that the cloud ceiling was pretty low, so our trip would likely be cut short, but we would be refunded for the difference or we could try to reschedule for another day, but there weren't any promises it would get better....our day was the first "good" flying day in a few days.

Being on a bit of a timeline, we opted to go ahead with it and were not disappointed. our pilot, Ace, was amazing. He talked to us along the way, gave all kinds of information about the area, pointed out rivers, glaciers, cabins, mountains whose names escape me. He was genuinely bummed that it wasn't clear enough for a glacier landing, he wanted us to experience that. Flying around, and probably through communicating with others, he "found a hole in the clouds..." and there we were, looking at the summit of Denali! Absolutely breathtaking.

Additionally, he pointed out part of a glacier that must have just calved and did an extra circle around.

By day's end, I had a credit back on my card - which was far more than anticipated, and I was glad I had tipped him (what I thought) well. We didn't start a stop watch on take off, so I really don't know how much time was missed. The fact that TAT took care of us so well ensures that we will certainly consider them first the next time we are in Talkeetna.

I never felt unsafe in the plane. Ace's expert flying skills were evident from take off to landing. Truly, I've felt much harder landings on much bigger planes. I only wish I had taken the time to ask how he got into flying, if he has favorite routes, learned a bit more about the hiker and skier drop offs - all things he would have told me if I hadn't left the plane with my family in complete awe of the experience.

Seats are tight. I'm a tall guy (6'7") and was glad for the space right by the door. It does get a little drafty on board, so if you are cold-sensitive, layer up.

Truly a lifetime highlight - and I can't wait to do it again.

Review Text: Booked this tour as I thought landing a plane on a glacier was just something I had to see for myself. The flight over the mountains and around Denali was thrilling with breathtaking views. Our pilot, a young man from New Zealand, was professional and knowledgable providing lots of information about the region. We saw Base Camp 2 at 11,000ft with a group of climbers camping. We also had 2 climbers on board who were going to be dropped at Base Camp to begin their summit attempt. Te landing at Bases Camp, 7,000 ft, was incredible. I highly recommend this excursion and would venture to say to should not be missed.

Review Text:
What an experience. We took this flight seeing tour from Talkeetna. Our time was 8.30 AM and we reached as required, around 45 minutes before. We did some paper work and were given a briefing about plane and safety. We were also given some boots to wear on our shoes when we land on glacier on the snow. We were three plus a few other people, totally around 9 passenger and two crew. It was a bit scary when we started but the beautiful scenes made us forget our fear. we were soon soaring over the trees, rivers, mountains, clouds and a lot more. What a beautiful trip, it was just awesome. The views were unbelievable. We went around a lot of peaks including magnificent Denali. Then the climax of our trip—landing on a glacier. It was just too good to be true. The pilot, a young chap from New Zealand landed very professionally. We got down on a fresh coat of snow. It was deep. We stayed there for around 20 minutes walking around and watching the scenery and taking pictures. Then it was time to take off again. Take off was also smooth and soon we’re up and circling the mountains again enjoying the ride and the views. Soon it was time to return to base. Overall an awesome experience.
Keep in mind this will be done if weather is clear. If not, then you get a full refund. We were lucky as last day it had snowed full day while our day was bright and sunny. This is an experience that is not to be missed.

Review Text:
We did the Mountain Voyager with Glacier Landing on June 19. We chose Talkeetna Air Taxi because Trip Advisor calls them "#1 of 35 Tours & Activities in Talkeetna". I called in March and spoke with Amy to discuss our flight options. Amy was great in taking the time to understand our situation and address our concerns. I told her my wife was a supplemental oxygen user and asked if there would be any issues. She told me we could not do the summit tour due to the height the plane flew, the need to user flight oxygen, and concerns about my wife's ability to quickly change from her oxygen concentrator to their air. Amy said we could do either Grand Denali or Mountain Voyager and recommended the glacier landing. I thanked her for her help and said i would be back to book in a couple weeks after we planned all our excursions for our stay in Talkeetna. We ultimately decided to fly Monday afternoon. When I returned to book I learned that many of their planes were reserved for summit landings that day and only the Mountain Voyager with Glacier Landing would be going out that afternoon. We booked that and are so happy we did.

Everyone was great from the time we arrived. The ladies there fitted us in landing suits with boots and helped put the boots on over our shoes. We flew with Liam. He gave is a safety briefing before we took off. The views we had early on were amazing. He did a soft touch down for the Glacier landing, and we spend about a half hour walking the glacier, watching another plane land. it started raining whine we were on the glacier. After we took off we flew a little more when Liam said because of weather he would have to cut the flight short and we would get refunds for the time we missed. I calculated that from the time we boarded the plane to touch down we were short 5 minutes, from take off to touch down we were short 10 minutes. Without our asking they refunded 15 minutes flight time. They couldn't have been more generous.

After landing, we asked for recommendations for something to eat. Not only did they give us a couple recommendations, but they gave us a ride to the one we chose. Thank you all at TAT.

Only issue - they sell t-shirts that are rolled-up in their office. When we got home my wife found her ladies medium was too snug and wished she bought a large.

Review Text: We did a Denali explorer flight seeing tour with glacier landing on July 5.  I had originally had this excursion booked for three weeks prior to this date, but I came down with covid and couldn't go on the cruise. We moved the cruise to a later date and I called Talkeetna Air Taxi to tell them and to ask if I could switch the excursion to the new date on my cruise and they were so helpful and understanding and made the change with no problem. I really appreciate how flexible and accommodating they were in this uncertain travel time that we are living in with Covid. When we arrived in Talkeetna we were asked to wait in front of a store on Main Street until we were picked up by one of their shuttle vans and brought to their office at the airfield. Once there we checked in, got our boot covers and waited for our flight time. We could see the plane that we were going to go up in and they were doing a last minute cleaning to it. Wiping down the windows to make sure everyone had a perfect view for pictures, which I thought was a nice touch. Finally our group was called to head to our plane where we met our pilot (I can’t remember his name, but he was from New Zealand and he was fantastic!). He went over the necessary safety information and then asked if anyone wanted to sit in the cockpit seat and of course I volunteered. That was the best decision, I got such amazing photos from up there which were unobstructed by the wings of the plane. We had a surprisingly clear day, we had even seen the mountain in her entirety from the ground so the pilot said we would have exceptional views once up at the mountain and boy was he right. There’s nothing that can compare to seeing the enormity and majesty of the range and that mountain up close. The pilot flew all around and switched directions so that both sides of the plane could get views of everything. He kept up a nice steady commentary of what we were seeing and interesting facts. Then it was time to land on the glacier. Our pilot picked Ruth Glacier to land because he said he liked the views from there better and I have to agree after seeing some of the other glacier landing sites that other pilots were using he was right. We were on the glacier for about 20 minutes to take photos, have a snowball fight, and just appreciate the beauty around us. He took photos of each family group with the plane, the mountain etc. I’m usually really picky about my photos and end up deleting most of them but I was pleasantly surprised with how perfect the photos he took were! We loaded back up in the plane and headed back to the airport. The whole ride was smooth with very little turbulence. Everyone that we met at Talkeetna Air Taxi was friendly and helpful. They are extremely professional and most importantly safe. Their equipment is maintained nicely. I can’t recommend this company enough.

Review Title: Flight and Glacier landing WORTH EVERY PENNY!
Review Text:
Grand Denali Tour with Glacier Landing---

I have traveled up through Talkeetna on to Denali National Park numerous times over the last 10 years. I had never, up until this trip, taken advantage of the Talkeetna Air Taxi service; and all I can say about that is "Shame on me!".
First, know that I have tried to take the flight out of Denali in the past. While I was not successful because of the weather, this trip I was advised that while the company out of the park is a great company, the flight into would potentially be better. The flight out saved 6 hours of bus time, and weather permitting saw some cool sights, but the flight in, with glacier landing would amaze. They were 100% right. Second, know that I was thinking of saving some money and not doing the glacier landing. I called Talkeetna Air and spoke with one of their employees. That employee did not pressure sell me at all. She explained what people like about the flight options, those with and without glacier landings, she gave me an honest account of the time in the air (15 minutes into the park, the a lot of time flying around the summit, then a landing if chosen, than a nice flight out) for a total time much longer than the flight out of the park (mind you). She also explained what she thinks of landing on the glacier. Explaining to me that while I have been to Alaska and hiked and seen glaciers, being on one in the Denali range in the mountains would amaze me with the vast openness and quite. Again, she didn't try to sell me, she simply tried to explain pros and cons. In the end, there weren't many cons other than a bit more money---and let's be honest, if you are forking out the money for the flight, you might as well not be cheap like I was going to be. We settled on the flight and landing and it was worth EVERY PENNY! I kid you not. Everything about the flight was amazing. Our pilot-- She was amazing. There was a time when she said--ok, we are going to fly into the face of the mountain now to give you an idea of how big it is--but don't worry, we are at least a mile from the face. It seemed like we were right next to it!! She warned us when it might get a bit bumpy, and why, and then we were prepared and could still experience the sights that the bumpy air allowed us to see. And the glacier landing was amazing. To land in snow in a mountain and take off in snow on a mountain is a modern feat. These planes they use are amazing. And the pilots the best! So there is that all by itself. But to step out and see it and listen and just exist was the best. Every person on that flight was blown away. Every person on that flight had a smile from ear to ear. I am not going to lie to you--- we had perfect weather on August 21st---some of the best they had seen in a couple of weeks. We saw Denali in all her beauty. In fact, we saw her driving in to Talkeetna, on the flight and the next day on the bus tour (which I have done 4 times and it never gets old). So we were blessed! But Talkeetna air does not shy away from being honest with you about the weather. They will not go up in the weather is bad. And if the clouds are in but weather ok to fly, they will be open about that tour. And they go out of their way to rebook you if necessary. In fact, later that week while in Seward on a whale/glacier tour with Alaska Saltwater Lodge & Tours (who I highly recommend as well) we met a mother and daughter that tried to fly the day before us. They could not because of weather. And Talkeetna worked with them and their very busy trip (already planned) to accommodate another flight. With that, what I recommend is you book your travel days (if going by car mind you) to Denali park a couple of days apart. Plan the flight on the way up there. If it doesn't work out, try to plan a reschedule for your day out of the area if going back towards Anchorage.

Bottom line-- I will absolutely do this experience again. I will absolutely use Talkeenta Air Taxi. I will absolutely do the flight and glacier landing. And I will absolutely love it.

Oh, and one other thing. I had my mom and dad with me. Both in the mid 70s. Mom a bit leery of small planes and nervous. She did fine. In fact, she did better than fine. She was not once scared nor flight sick nor anything but amazed. It was one of the highlights of her trip and it set the stage for more adventures.

Thank you Talkeetna Air!

Review Title: Would give it 10 stars if I could!
Review Text: Our family took this flight with a glacier landing. I wrestled with whether to do the landing or not and decided to go ahead and book it knowing that many times they get cancelled. The day of our flight was cloudy but had no rain. When we arrived they told us that the earlier flight had been cancelled due to visibility, but ours would be able to fly. Since there was a lot of cloud cover in the lower elevations we would not be able to land though. We were given the choice to cancel or reschedule, but it would have been difficult to fit it into our schedule on another day. Besides, the next time might be worse. We decided to go ahead and go and were assured that we would still have good views once we got above the clouds.  We seemed to be flying in complete clouds for a few minutes and I thought it was going to be a bust and then we broke through the clouds and wow! As we flew around up there the clouds seemed to dissipate and the next thing we knew the pilot said it had cleared so much that we were going to be able to land!  It was a very smooth landing on snow and we landed at base camp where the hikers start their journey to climb Denali. It was absolutely amazing to stand there among those majestic mountains. Words cannot even describe it. We had plenty of time to take photos and walk around. You could go pretty far if you wanted and there were cones set up that you were not to go past. Then back on the plane and were heading down the hill and rather than the plane lifting up it was like the ground just falls away from the plane. You feel so close to the huge mountains, but they said we were still 10 miles away at least! The pilot was very experienced, the flight and landing very smooth, and pilot communicated with us through headsets. Facemasks are requred due to covid. It was an amazing experience for our family and in my opinion a must-do in Alaska if you have the funds.

Review Text: My girlfriend and I spent two weeks traveling throughout Alaska, and this was the highlight of our trip (it was even better than catching a 60lb halibut in Prince William Sound). Denali dwarfs the surrounding 14'er peaks, and it makes for a very humbling experience flying from 300' above sea level to the base of Denali in roughly 25 minutes. My girlfriend is a nervous flier, and our pilot made her feel extremely safe. She explained that she is a mother and she had been flying since she was a kid. It instilled a soothing sense of anxiety relief. The plane seated 10 persons total, and it was a very smooth flight. The plane had modern avionics, and it was very clean. Both these factors lead us to believe the plane was well maintained and safe. The glacier landing was well worth the upgrade cost. It made for a great photo opportunity. The shear rock faces double those of Yosemite, and the deep blues on the glaciers cannot be replicated through photos. Our pilot was knowledgeable of the geography in the area, and the flight path enables great views for passengers on both sides of the plane. 10 out of 10 would recommend!

Review Title: Awe-inspiring flightseeing with glacier landing, and heli-hiking
Review Text:
Alaska is awe-inspiring no matter which way you turn, but our flightseeing trip with a glacier landing with TAT in Denali National Park was a once-in-a-lifetime experience. The group included our family of 3 plus 3 other passengers. Our pilot provided information about the aircraft as well as the geography, and pointed out specific rivers, glaciers and mountains as we flew among them. He also pointed out several of the camps for the climbers and rangers on Denali. The vantage point of flying through mountain passes and around peaks was breathtaking. It seemed as if you could reach out and touch the rock faces despite the fact that they were miles away. Landing on the glacier at over 5000' elev. was incredible. Amazing to think we were standing on many feet of snow and a couple thousand feet of ice. It was so quiet and peaceful in the bowl where we landed and we felt so small among the towering peaks.
We also took a TAT helicopter for a heli-hiking trip into the Talkeetna Mountains. It was amazing hovering over the rivers and lakes and the tundra, spotting a moose, and landing in the high country for a guided hike. Everyone at TAT was welcoming and professional. We highly recommend them.

Review Text: We booked the 1.5 hour Southside Explorer w/Glacier Landing tour for 6 adults. We called Talkeetna Air when we arrived in Talkeetna. Because our train did not let us out at the train station there was some confusion as to where to pick us up. After a few phone calls we were picked up and taken to their office at the airport. When we went inside we were told the owner was checking the weather. They told us it would be too windy for the glacier landing. We could cancel the flight and get a 100% refund or get a 30 minute longer flight to the North Range. We decided to take the longer flight. Although we were disappointed that we did not land on a glacier safety is their main concern and we understood that. After paying the final payment we went outside to get our glacier boots, just in case. We walked to the plane and met our pilot. He gave us a safety talk and told us some things about the plane. We all boarded and biu on our headsets and seatbelts. The headsets did not have a microphone so we could not communicate with each other. We had a very smooth takeoff. The flight was very smooth except when we went over a mountain. Nothing to worry about. Flying over the glaciers and snow cover peaks is just amazing. It looks like you can reach out and touch them but the pilot said we were at least a mile away. After flying over the North Range the pilot swung around and took us over College Fjord. The cool thing about this was the day before we were in the fjord on the Golden Princess cruise ship. What a beautiful way to see everything!

Review Title: Fantastic Views - Denali up close and perssonal
Review Text:
We took the Grand Denali tour with a Glacier Landing. The plane held 9 passengers. 8 passengers each had a window seat, and the 9th passenger sat in the copilot seat. Our pilot, LeAnn, did a fantastic job. She would make turns to make sure each side of the plane got the great views and pictures. Because of the size of the mountains, it looked like the plane was way to close to them, but LeAnn assured us that she was always at least a mile from them. She pointed out places and told us what was going on (like before we turned). She was in constant communication with the pilots on other tours checking in with the weather conditions,

The views were awe experiencing. Make sure you bring a memory card with space for a lot of pictures! The Glacier Landing was impressive. We landed at Base Camp, which is the first camp that mountaineers use to climb Denali. It is in the middle of the 3 highest mountains.

We were lucky that the weather was great to allow us to fly around Denali and do the Glacier Landing (they provide pull over boots and sunglasses for the Glacier). Be aware, that like most things with flying, mother nature controls where the plan can go. Realize that the flight you reserved may be changed. FOr example, you may not be able to fly all around Denali or do the Glacier Landing (they stopped doing Glacier Landings after ours). If your trip is changed, the office will alter your charges, appropriately.

One thing to note, if you are in an Otter with 9 passengers, I recommend that you do not jump for the copilot seat. Unless you are really tall, the Otter flies in a nose up configuration, so it is actually harder to see things.

It was a great trip. I would highly recommend it.

Review Title: Fabulous experience and guess who flew us...
Review Text: Anyone visiting Alaska always hear about doing their once in a life time flightseeing Denali tour including glacier landing that most of these tours do. I came across this recommendation all along on my web search as well as in all the conversations with friends who’ve visited Alaska. I took a chance by not booking the tour in advance and started my search right after we checked in to Talkeetna. I inquired with a couple of flightseeing tour operators including K2 which seems to be quite popular on the web. My web search greatly influenced me to go with K2 (superb marketing) and I decided to go with them. I stepped into their office and checked for availability, unfortunately they didn’t have any tours with glacier landing that day and I felt so bad for not booking in advance. I had spotted a small corner office of Talkeetna Air Taxi on the way so I went there but bad luck again, it was locked. I decided to call them on the number listed on their office window and that’s when things started to change, for better. Within a few minutes of my call they booked us with Glacier landing and surprisingly with a better price (than K2), thanks to children discounts, now we’ve to rush to their base office as our appointment was just about 30 mins away. We quickly changed clothes and reached the base office on time, everything went perfect from that point onwards, the sweet lady at the counter took some info, weighed us on scale, handed a colored ticket and asked us to step out and wait for our plane. We were given snow shoe covers and within a few minutes we were greeted by a gentlemen called “Paul”. Paul was our pilot and we quickly mingled with him as he seemed to be quite an international traveler with varied experiences from across continents. Paul was super nice with us, sharing lot of meaningful information throughout the plane ride and helped us took pictures on the glacier. We all were very much impressed with Paul’s service and loved the flight experience from beginning to end. Paul safely got us back on ground and we were still awestruck with the beauty of Denali and our flightseeing experience. While returning the snow shoe covers I told the shoe staff that Paul was such an amazing pilot and he quickly responded, yeah he’s an amazing person and he’s the owner of Talkeetna Air Taxi, wow, now we’re even more thrilled knowing who flew us to Denali and our memories suddenly became even more precious. Thank you Paul and Talkeetna Air Taxi, you guys rock and I’ll recommend each and every Alaska tourist to add you guys to their Alaska memories. You’ll not be disappointed, if the owner is so friendly and professional then you can imagine how professional other staff would be. As many other reviewers said this was indeed THE highlight of our 3 weeks Alaska adventure.

Review Text: Well worth the money – and the best money spent was the $50 fee for the glacier landing. If you are going to pay nearly $400 for the ride, pay the extra $50 and land on the glacier.    The planes have headsets and the pilot talks about what you are seeing explaining glaciers, receding glaciers, areas that look like there is no glacier as they are completely gray but under that is glacier, etc.   It is very noisy without the headsets.   Our pilot, Clay, explains what mountain, glacier, etc. you are seeing.  He even made sure both sides of the plane got to see Mt. McKinley.  All the seats faced forward, and the wing was overhead.  It added to the pictures having a little wing in the picture to give perspective.   I took our GoPro and suction cupped it to the wall of the airplane, so it pivoted out over the window and let it run on its own. The videos are awesome!  If you don’t have a GoPro and are going on this flight, this flight alone is worth buying one!   I also rented a 400mm lens to go on our camera.  I used it, but, since you are so close to most things, the 200mm and even the 55mm lens was good. Actually, as close as we were to Mt. McKinley my cell phone took a great picture.  We didn’t have great views of Denali as it was covered in clouds, but, did get a pretty good view and picture.   The flight was very safe/smooth, and our pilot was very diligent in explaining the safety precautions involved in the flight.

We booked the tour in advance so we showed up 30 minutes early as requested and we were quickly checked in. You have to be weighed with everything you're taking with you but no one sees the weight except the person behind the counter. Review Title: Better the weather, better the experience.
Review Text: We had a clear day. Rare, I'm told. The experience was amazing. To float above, among, between and land on the Denali mountain range with a photo to be had every 20 seconds makes you go 'should I not just be looking and soakin' it all in?' or 'shouldn't I be taking every photo I can?'For those who choose looking and soaking, then bring your polaroid glasses, it gets bright up there with all that snow, not to mention clouds. If you are landing on the glacier then sunburn cream is a good idea to wear, and take gloves and hat to keep your ears warm (it'll be 5-10 degrees colder than at the airport).For those who choose taking every photo you can, then a polaroid filter will bring out the best shots. Also if you can sit up the front this is definitely the time to use your panorama photo feature on your phone as you'll get front and side views that can only be captured this way, unless you have really wide angle lense. The advantage of not sitting up the front is that your windows are not curved and your camera can focus a whole lot easier on your subject. If there are two of you going on this trip make sure you sit on either side of the aisle so you can get different shots, you can share them later.Generally the air is smooth, its not the tropics with air rising and getting turbulent, this is cold air not doing much. But if you are airsick prone, looking through a camera eyepiece looking at land in motion, with the airplane turning will only make you more airsick sensitive. My advice (being a pilot)   in that regard is to a) take your motion sickness tablet at least half hour before take off b) have something in your stomach already ie breakfast or lunch b) take a piece of candy you can suck on the first time you get a hint of sickness c) take pictures angled forward rather than directly out the side (sense of motion is less) d) don't take pictures when the plane banks. e) look at the horizon after every photo to get your sense of up or down reset in your mind.Last suggestion, for those who put their pictures into photo books, you might want to take a few pictures of the video being played in the snow shoe fitting area. The shots I took were of the aircraft flying and landing on the glacier. These are going to be difficult to get in real life and will be handy for your photo story. This trip on a clear day is a must do for those who appreciate Gods handiwork, for those who love geography, for those who love flying and mostly for those who love photography.

Review Title: Its all about pleasing the customer!
Review Text:
I'm so impressed with their service and willingness to accommodate the needs of their clients. This is so rare and a great value. Read on!

This company was recommended by the pilot with Stellar Aviation in Homer. He said a lot of excellent Pilots have gone over to this company. We also chatted with an air traffic controller who told us that the larger, flashier companies have a higher turnover of Pilots.

They have multiple planes including a four seater and 10 seater. They are flexible on their pricing. They will adjust their pricing based on what you are to see of Denali. This is amazing. They also let you cancel if it looks like the mountain is not going to be visible and you decide you don't want to go. Special boots are provided for the people who go on flights that have a glacier landing. And if you're lucky, you might be added onto one of those flights even though you were paying for just a fly by. Again, amazing! I also learned that even if it's only one person who wants to fly, they would take you out and would not increase the cost to offset the fact that you're the only person. But honestly, I think they do such a great job it is likely a rare event when there's only one person to go.

The flight was wonderful. The pilot made sure that everyone on the plane had equal opportunity to see everything. We appreciated his narration which was more than adequate. It was relaxed and informative. He gave some historic background about the first hikers, the naming of Denali, Etc.

They were so efficient, helpful, and accommodating. It's rare to see a business so willing to work with the needs of the client and be affordable at the same time. I wouldn't consider going with any other company after this experience.

A side note: we talked on the phone about the pricing. This is where we learned that based on how much of the mountain we would see, the price would be adjusted. We also learned there was a 10% discount if you book online.

Review Text:
My family and I recently flew on the 1.25 hour Denali flight with Talkeetna Air Taxi flight when the weather in Anchorage prevented flying from there. My mom really wanted to fly the mountain while here, and so we called and asked if they might have availability for a large group of 6 on short notice. I have an interesting perspective of this flight because I fly commercial seaplanes off of Lake Hood in Anchorage and my company does our own Denali tours, so it was actually about my 15th flight of the mountain. The flight really helped familiarize me with the mountain and offered new and unknown routes that I had not previously flown. We also learned a lot of history and information about the mountain that I can share with passengers of my own. The day right after flying with TAT I found myself giving a Denali on the mountain retracing our steps. I learned a lot from Matt, our pilot, and am very grateful for his insights about flying the mountain.

Matt was happy to answer questions from both myself and my family, and they really enjoyed their experience. I can not thank him enough for helping me better chart and conduct my own tours of the mountain. Beautiful airplanes, beautiful scenery, and engaging pilots (I flew with these guys last year as well). If you want to start your Denali tour while in Talkeetna, these guys are awesome.

Review Text:
The flight-seeing tour of Denali was the highlight of our trip to Alaska --- and that's saying a lot! We were originally scheduled for an afternoon flight on the day after our arrival in AK; when we arrived in Talkeetna, the view of Denali was obscured by clouds, and we began to worry about whether visibility would be good enough for the flight (not from the safety perspective but from a viewing/picture-taking perspective). The check-in staff offered us an opportunity to speak with the pilot who was due back from the tour we were about to take to get first-hand information about current weather conditions on the mountain. The pilot said that the peaks were obscured by clouds, and indicated that the weather for the following day was expected to be clearer (but of course, no one really knows what the weather will be from one day --- or even one hour --- to the next). We decided to postpone our flight until the following morning, and as advertised, the staff was fully supportive of our decision and did not make us feel bad about backing out at the last moment.

Our decision to wait until the following morning was richly rewarded. The weather was beautiful and the visibility was fantastic! Our pilot, Shiloh, was excellent. He provided great information on everything we were seeing and the flight was flawless --- very smooth and designed to give us an opportunity to get great views/great pictures. We then took off and flew back to Talkeetna with no issues at all.

There is no way I would send someone to Alaska without forcing them to do this tour. If you do not do this, you are missing out on a truly once of a lifetime experience (unless you are one of the pilots, who get to do this amazing thing every single day).

Review Title: Bet Way to See Denali and a Glacier
Review Text:
We took the 11am flight around Denali and land on a glacier. I can’t imagine a better way to see the mountain and get a sense for how big it is!

We had 5 total in our plane (including the pilot). The pilot did an excellent job describing the landscape and giving us a sense for the vast expanse we were flying over.

We rose to about 12,000 feet on a party cloudy day. We saw incredible views the entire way, including the peak of Denali. We were also able to see one of the base camps of the mountain climbers who were about halfway to the top.

As amazing as seeing Denali up close, landing on the glacier made the trip for us. After a smooth landing, we walked on untouched snow which sat on top of about 2,000 feet of ice. Because of how high the mountains are (granite walls rising 5,000 feet) I found it almost impossible to put anything into perspectives that my mind can comprehend. When we listened quietly, we could hear small landslides occurring on the granite shelves.

We had some issues with our schedule and the folks at Talkeetna were extremely accommodating. Overall the service and experience were excellent from beginning to end!

Quick tips: we went on a warm day (70 degrees Fahrenheit) and were glad to have a decent jacket in the plane and on the glacier. Also we wore hiking boots and didn’t need to borrow the shoe covers. Sitting up front in the plane is terrific, but the curvature of the plane glass will limit some of the photo opportunities (at least straight on). You can still take photos through the side windows while sitting up front.

Review Text:
A friend and I flew with Talkeetna Air Taxi in June and LOVED it. A flightseeing tour of Denali had come highly recommended by someone who had visited Alaska before, so we splurged on the activity.

We chose the Southside Explorer + Glacier Landing tour... Our guess was that the views we'd see from any of the other tours would be marginally the same but that adding the glacier landing would greatly add to the experience. So by saving $ by choosing the cheaper tour, we felt more justified in paying extra for the glacier landing.

It was worth it!!!! The glacier landing was the coolest part of the trip. Keep in mind that the planes might not always be able to land on the glaciers depending on weather. When we checked in before our flight, they warned us that we might not be able to land because weather near the glacier had not allowed them to land all day. They said that if we weren't able to land, they would reimburse us for the additional glacier landing cost. We were so lucky that the weather actually DID allow us to land, and I am so glad they did. The boots that they give you kept our shoes and socks dry (they easily fit over your shoes and have gaiters that cinch up on your calves.)

We were also lucky that day that we were able to see the mountain. A layer of cloud over was chopping off the top of Denali from the ground, but our pilot was able to climb above the cloud cover to give us a view of Denali and its neighboring peaks from above the clouds. Mesmerizing!! I speculated that the pilot was able to get the plane that high because our tour only had 5 people including the pilot so the plane weighed less. I wonder if a more crowded tour would have been able to do that? Might be worth asking them that, and if that is true, then I would recommend taking a less popular trip to maximize your chances that you'd be in a plane that could climb high enough to see the peak.

Worth the splurge!

Our pilot was very familiar with the area and offered a detailed narration during the flight. During our landing, he was able to elaborate in as much more detail.

Talkeetna Air Taxi has been doing this for a long time and it shows in their efficiency and professionalism. Everyone we interacted with from booking the reservation to getting off the plane were very friendly, down-to-earth and professional. They all had great energy, which added to our excitement for the trip. Two members of my group got to sit in the co-pilot's seat (one going out and one coming back) which made their trip all the more memorable.

TAT very generously offered our active duty military group a discount, which they certainly didn't have to do, especially at the height of the flying season. They entire operation has a very relaxed, community atmosphere, which is how things are supposed to be in that part of Alaska. They generously share that attitude and experience with their customers in every aspect of thrip. I hope to go up with them again when my kids get old enough in a couple years.

Review Title: Tremendous Experience - Even with a Major Disappointment
Review Text:
Our flight-seeing experience started in downtown Talkeetna at the cozy information/reservation office. There the representative used a cool 3D map of the mountain range to show us exactly where each of the tour options went and what was included in each. He was exceptionally helpful in describing all aspects of the tours, comparing and contrasting them and offering insights regarding the day’s weather and its possible impact on the flights. We ultimately chose the Grand Denali Tour and received directions to the Air Taxi airfield.

When we arrived to check in, we filled out the paperwork, were weighed in (the planes have a weight limit), and were directed to the storage area for the glacier boots. We told the desk person that we did not reserve a glacier landing tour. She whisked us outside and explained in hushed tones that we were being upgraded – no extra charge. They had a glacier flight that was not full; we would complete the seating (if we didn’t mind). We didn’t!

So far, so good. We got our boots and relaxed on the large deck overlooking the airstrip. We waited and watched a constant parade of planes take off and land. And we waited. And we waited. For more than an hour we waited our turn while clouds gathered around the mountains in the distance. By the time we boarded our plane, the gorgeous day with wide-open blue skies had turned gray and the “seeing” part of our flight-seeing tour was in jeopardy.

Sure enough, by the time our plane arrived near Denali, the pilot told us the visibility was too bad for us to make a close approach and fly-around of the mountain. I could not help but think, “There’s a thousand bucks down the toilet.”

Nonetheless, we veered off and made our way to Mt. Foraker, the second largest of the mountains, as well as Mt. Hunter, the third largest. We flew close in to both and along the way traversed mountain valleys, zoomed over other peaks and followed glacial paths, viewing the brilliant colors, the deep crevasses and the sparkling open waters that dotted the tops. Each bank around a mountain’s edge brought more awe-inspiring scenery. As we dove down into another pass, our pilot announced our descent toward the glacier. As one side of the mountain pass opened below us, we could see a makeshift airfield at the far end of a second valley. We turned toward the site and were soon skimming over the snow and ice, taxiing in next to several other tourist planes.

I’m from Michigan. I’ve seen my share of snow. I’ve wandered wilderness areas in the winter. This, however, was other-worldly (think Hoth from Star Wars). We were surrounded by towering cliffs on three sides, with added rivers of snow flowing down between edges, adding to the mass we were on. We walked about the glacier for about a half hour, taking photos, watching other planes take off and land and learning glacier facts from our pilot. Before leaving, our pilot took photos of everyone and gave us the itinerary for the remainder of our flight.

Taking off from the glacier was an experience. First, we were heading downhill, as the glacier was flowing downward into the large valley we turned from originally. The glacier’s edge dropped off precipitously into the valley, so we had only a limited amount of “runway” – kind of like flying off an aircraft carrier. Lastly, the air currents were dramatically different inside the valley, and they would hit the plane perpendicularly as we flew off the edge of our glacier and into the larger chasm. Fun.

Believe it or not, it was! How often do you get to experience something like that? Our pilot lifted off and arced into the valley and quickly ascended above the valley walls. Before we knew it, the entire range was again below us and the green flatlands surrounding Talkeetna beckoned us back to the airfield. As an extra on the way back, we saw a large brown bear walking along the shoreline of one of the many lakes below.

Once back on the ground, our pilot told us that we would be compensated for the disappointment of not viewing Denali – we’d all be getting a partial refund. In our case, this was pretty sweet, as we’d already received a free upgrade. The refund was substantial, too, so it made the overall experience all the better, knowing that the company treated their customers that fairly.

Even without seeing the star of the show, the Talkeetna Air Taxi flight-seeing experience was one I’ll never forget. They have to get a demotion for the long delay between check-in and take-off, which ultimately caused us to miss the view of the summit; however, everything else was absolutely first class. The sales staff and airfield personnel were friendly and professional. Our pilot was excellent and a fine tour guide, too, and Mother Nature set an incredible table for us to enjoy. I felt completely safe and comfortable in the plane, and the headphones worked very well to both reduce engine noise and provide the pilot’s commentary.

As alluded to earlier, this is not an inexpensive experience. Unless you have a sizeable disposable income, this will likely be a once-in-a-lifetime kind of thing, but it is certainly one to consider, and I think well worth the price – especially if you have a camera with a ton of memory. Anecdotally, I’ve heard that Talkeetna Air Taxi is considered the better of the flight-seeing tours available, and I found nothing that might argue the point. If you get the chance, open the wallet and fly off into the wild blue yonder. You will not regret it (unless you forget that camera).

Review Text:
Our party of four booked the Southside Explorer (one hour flight plus glacier landing). When we arrived that morning we received a weather briefing and learned the glacier landing would not be possible if we departed at the scheduled time. We were presented with options i.e. flight only (glacier landing component of booking to be refunded), wait 45 minutes to see if weather would permit a landing, get a complete refund, or rebook for later in the day. We decided to wait after which time we learned the glacier landing would be highly unlikely but the low cloud would not impact views of the mountains. We decided to go ahead and were fitted with the glacier landing gear just in case.

The flight was smooth and the views of the mountains were fantastic. It felt like we were extremely close to the mountains but the pilot assured us we would never be less than 1/4 mile from the face of the mountains. Our pilot was excellent ensuring each side of the plane enjoyed the views. We flew to the glacier landing area and could see it wasn't possible to land. Honestly, the flight was so good we were happy not to land (and receive a refund for that portion).

We highly recommend Talkeetna for their professionalism and for ensuring we had the best possible experience.

Review Text:
I booked the Mountain Voyager tour with Talkeetna Air Taxi over Labor Day. I got into town earlier the day before than originally planned so I stopped in to see if they had anything later that day. I found out that there was an opening in a tour later that afternoon so I rescheduled. They knew that they were going to be able to do that tour, but the next day could have been an issue. The weather changes all the time so you never know for sure, but TAT does their best to get their tours to be able to go but not risk anyone's safety.

The tour with the glacial landing was scheduled to be about 1 3/4 hours, but they don't hurry things and we took a little more than 2 hours. While heading out to a glacier to do the landing you get to see some excellent views of the Talkeetna area and the area up to the Alaska Range. We had eight people in the plane which I believe is one of the larger planes. Everyone gets to have a window seat since they are single seats with an aisle. You may even be lucky enough to get a chance to ride in the co-pilots seat. I have to say that I've never seen such beautiful views on the flight. The pilot attempts to provide everyone a great view and gives some great information as you get to the landing site.

The glacier landing was fantastic. You get to leave then exit the plane and walk around the glacial area. There were several other TAT planes there also enjoying the views. You spend about 15 minutes or so on the glacier so you have plenty of time for pics and videos, along with snowball fight if you are there with a group (there was fresh snow the day we were there). They provide you with boots you put over your shoes for walking around the glacier.

When we took off from the glacier that was even amazing. Even on our flight back the pilot gave us information on things we were passing over.

I would recommend this tour to anyone that wants to do something different and get to see great sites. The staff at TAT was excellent to work with always keeping your informed.

Review Text:
My now hubby...has never been on a plane!! And all he ever wants to do is fly...so Talkeetna Air Taxi and i did just that, we surprised him!! I have never seen him so excited, full of love and laughter as he was up there in the air. Our pilot was great and taught us a lot about glaciers and the landscape of Alaska. Most definitely take the flight if you can! We couldn't land on the glacier due to new snow fall, but it was still breath-taking.

Word of advice to my fellow motion sickness pals...Bonine! I used to use Dramamine but got turned on to Bonine, take it the night before and the morning of and good to go! A couple times while flying over the mountains and taking turns so all aboard can see the magnificent scenery almost had me evacuate my breakfast. But Bonine and me kept it under control (even went halibut fishing later in the trip and 3 people on board threw up...but not me!!! I still had to focus on keeping nausea at bay, but I did it!)

I said to my wife, "we're doing it."

As for the discomfort, the truth is, you are either going to get killed or you are going to have the ride of a lifetime, and the odds of getting killed are very very low. So, do it.

Review Text:
My husband and I had a great trip with Talkeetna Air Taxi. We booked over the phone and were given the tip that sometimes they have to cancel flights due to weather so to be flexible. We booked for a 3:15, with plans to stay overnight in Talkeetna just in case we needed to delay to later that night or to possibly the next morning. When we arrived they had to cancel a lot of their morning flights and weren't doing the Mountain Voyager (which is the one we signed up for). They also hadn't been able to land on a glacier yet that day and weren't sure if our tour would be able to. They offered us to switch to a 6:30 tour if we wanted to wait. We did decide to wait and wandered around town for a few hours. When we came back for our 6:30 tour they still weren't doing the Mountain Voyager but they had just had some planes land on the glacier, we decided to take that one instead of waiting for the 8:30 the next morning which was also offered to us. They gave us a refund for the additional cost of the longer tour since we took the shorter one just on the south side, and it was a very easy experience.

The scenery is stunning, worth every penny. We did get to land on a glacier and it was great. On our way out, Denali had started to clear so I'm pretty sure our pilot took some extra time to turn the plane back and forth so we could all get pictures of Denali. He had mentioned that it hadn't been out of the clouds all day.

The tour itself is great, but to be honest the most impressive thing to me was the customer service here. The women behind the desk we dealt with were so nice, especially considering they have to tell people everyday that their tour has been cancelled, shortened, no glacier landings etc. I can't imagine it is easy for them, but their friendly attitude is probably the only reason I took the time to write a review! Everyone else can tell you how awesome the flight and glacier are, but the staff makes this company worth spending your money.

Review Text: Yes, it is expensive, and yes, I believe it worth every penny. At least it was for us. Those flights are very weather dependent, the flight could be cancelled, the flight plan could be shortened (ours was, we've got the Mountain Voyager instead of booked Grand Denali, because of the weather conditions north of the Denali peak). The glacier landing could also be cancelled (ours wasn't). If it happens to you, don't blame the company. Your safety is a paramount for them. Personally I was impressed with high professionalism of the company staff and especially the pilot (we had Richard with us). The reservation was easy, the cancellation policy is reasonable and refunds if needed are quick and easy. Everything they told us was right on the mark. Glacier landing is well worth extra 95 bucks. We felt very safe during the flight, motion sickness was not an issue and the scenery was out of this world. Alaska Range is unlike any other mountain ranges I have seen before. The glaciers are enormous and the whole area is as wild as it gets. Besides if you are visiting Alaska and your time is limited this is your best chance to see Denali peak. Actually this is the only chance to see it up close unless you are actually climbing a mountain in Alaska Range. But even in that case you probably will be taking Talkeetna Air Taxi flight anyway to save a week of walking to the base camp. We actually saw the Denali base camp while flying over the glacier (just a few tents left as it was the end of the climbing season). Regarding the views and seating I think all seats have good views, but if you are a couple and both are planning to take pictures, seat on the opposite sides as the views are a bit different. By the way you don't need/want to have completely clear skies for your flight. Some clouds make the scenery even more beautiful. If you want to get some feeling on how it looks up there or just check the views and the weather/visibility conditions before your flight, there is an FAA webcam site for Alaska. The bottom line: I do recommend the flight and the company to do it with. This is not your average helicopter flight with glacier landing. This is a very special flight you cannot take anywhere in the world. We really enjoyed our tour, took a ton of pictures and video as the scenery was superb.

our group of ten was on way to Denali and decided to stop by and book the glacier landing tour last minute. Fortunately they were able to accommodate us. It's expensive but well worth the money. Everybody in the group were thrilled. Spectacular views on plane and there is enough time allowed on glacier for snowball fight and lots of photos.

Review Text:
Based on TripAdvisor recommendation we booked it in advance with Talkeetna Air Taxi. But we learned  that price remained same at last moment. There is another company K-2 aviation, it shares same compound for operation and have many planes and their car parking was also full.

We took Alaskan tour bus from Denali for our return journey to Anchorage. We had break journey at Talkeetna. They picked us from  Talkeetna Alaska lodge and dropped. We had enough time on hand and he allowed us to take break in downtown for Lunch and in return for dinner.

Cabins are non pressurised. So I felt a little ear popping which was manageable by moving jaws and mint. It is advisable to keep mint handy. We were given booties for glacier landing.

 It was clear day. The views from plane was great. Landing on the glacier was a breathe taking experience and being on the glacier (15min) was one of the coolest parts.Once in a lifetime must do. Pilot narrated things on the way making the trip as enjoyable by explaining what we see and taking pictures for everyone on landing on Pika glacier.  If you're on the fence about this trip because of the price, don't be--it's worth every penny.

Overall, I am glad we did it.

We were treated to unparalleled views of "mini Switzerland", the west buttress of Denali and finally the Sheldon Amphitheater and upper Ruth Gorge where we landed and spent a glorious, 30 mins playing in the snow, enjoying bright sunshine and soaking in the sheer beauty of this place.
One special commendation to Talkeetna Air Taxi for being such a safe and thoughful operator - we were given snow boots to cover our sneakers and a great check in briefing. Richard, our pilot, provided everyone on the plane with great photo angles by adjusting the flight route to capture vistas from both sides of the aircraft - there really were no bad views on the plane and his commentary was spot on! We have no hesitation recommending this trip - it really is a must do activity for your "bucket list", even if you live in Alaska!

Review Text:
We recently enjoyed a flight with Talkeetna Air Taxi that included a glacier landing. It's hard to describe how much fun and how exciting the entire flight was. Of course the scenery was spectacular. The view of the peaks of Denali, Foraker and Hunter, white with snow and protruding from a solid layer of clouds was breathtaking. It is a toss up whether the views of Denali or the glacier landing was the most exciting - both provided memories for years to come. Our flight was in the afternoon and the office building at the airport was very busy with travelers awaiting flights as well as those who had just returned. Although busy, the entire process was well organized and simple. There was noticeable positive energy and excitement in both groups. All the staff we met were knowledgeable, friendly, and eager to make our experience memorable. Our pilot, Dave, was highly experienced, confident, thorough, and really fun. His description of what we were seeing as well as what maneuvers he was going to do, gave us, the passengers, a high degree of comfort. Plus he provided a lot of good information on glaciers and the geography of Alaska. We flew in a turboprop, De Havilland Otter that seated eight-or-so passengers plus the pilot. The glacier landing was so exciting as the pilot didn't have to descend to land...he just flew until the skis of the aircraft landed on the snowy upward slope which served to slow the aircraft down to taxi speed very quickly...and, it was so quiet as we landed - a truly unique experience.
After about 15 or 20 minutes in the snow outside the aircraft, taking photos and watching two other aircraft land on the glacier, we re-boarded and the pilot pointed the nose down the snowy slop and we glided downhill until we were once again airborne. Our flight was capped by the fact that upon returning to the Talkeetna area, we had to circle the airfield until a moose that had wandered onto the runway decided to move back into the woods. I venture to guess that most of us had never before had a landing delayed by a wandering moose. A bit expensive, yes...worth the cost, most definitely! Flying with Talkeetna Air Taxi was, without a doubt, one of the highlights of our visit to Alaska. This company and its people have earned our highest recommendation. Just do it...you'll be very glad that you did!

Review Text:
I booked the Mountain Voyager with Glacier Landing flight with Talkeetna Air Taxi. While traveling from Wasilla to Talkeetna, I spotted Denali in the distance -- this was an exciting start to the day. After checking in at the office, I put some booties on over my shoes and boarded the aircraft. The craft seated ten passengers, and we all had windows. Headsets helped to muffle the engine noise and hear from our pilot (the microphones were not activated). The weather was clear as we headed into the Alaska range, but we encountered some clouds/mist as we first entered the mountains. It was hard to see, and I had to remind myself that these pilots fly these routes every day and weren't going to fly the plane into the side of a mountain! Thankfully, the clouds cleared soon. The views of the snow, ice, and glaciers below were stunning. Now and then, we'd get a glimpse of bright blue ice below. Then we spotted the peaks of Denali -- the the highest mountain peak in North America. One of the main reasons I took this flight was to increase my chances of seeing it, and fate was on my side this day. It was breathtaking to see the crisp white snow against a brilliant blue sky, with its own little cloud on top. I had lots of time to snap some photos and video as we slowly moved from north to east peaks.
We landed on Ruth Glacier, where we all stepped out on to the snowy surface (thank goodness for the booties)! We had ample time to walk around a bit and take photos. There were maybe a half dozen other planes around, and it was interesting to watch them take off and land. I had a moment that literally took my breath away when I took a step and my foot sunk down about 18" beneath the snow! But I laughed as I was startled, and was not hurt in any way. We were also able to get a few more glimpses of Denali as the clouds just beneath the mountain top shifted in the light breeze.
I could not have asked for a better experience -- well worth the price and a memory that will be a highlight of my first time in Alaska!!

Review Text: We made reservations with Talkeetna Air Taxi in October 2016 for our "Great Alaska Vacation" in June 2017. The flight around Denali with a glacier landing was one of the most anticipated items on our itinerary. We knew there was a risk of weather causing a problem and sadly it did. We arrived for our morning flight with scattered showers and overcast skies. TAT showed how they monitored a web cam and communicated with climbers to assess the conditions. Denali was not flyable, but they gave us three afternoon times. When we came back TAT was "straight as an arrow" with us. With eight pilots waiting around, they really wanted to fly. Our experience was most important to them however, and they said we would not see much on the flight. Alas, no Denali this time, but we hope to come back. If we make it back we will absolutely schedule Talkeetna Air Taxi. We'll probably add a "Plan B" day in case of weather! Good, TRUSTWORTHY folks!!

Yes, the weather may play foul and ruin your plans but it's worth the risk to reserve a day for this once-in-a lifetime experience. Our pilot LeeAnn, a resident of Talkeetna, was very experienced and amicable. She gave a running commentary of the regional landscape while flying safely. We have never seen (and doubt if we shall ever see again) mountains, glaciers, walls of granite, the great Wickersham wall from such close proximity. With the sun shining brightly upon us, it was unusually warm on the glacier. Talkeetna Air Taxi crew provide the necessary footgear to walk on the glacier. It was pure and pristine, to the extent, that we could just pick up snow from the glacier to quench our thirst! The 360 degree landscape is mindblowingly beautiful and it will always be the most beautiful Alaskan memory for us to cherish!

Review Title: Spectacular Denali flight and glacier landing
Review Text:
Very efficient check in process but weather looked sketchy. Met our pilot, Leighanne, who looks 19 but assured us she was 37, a mom and a a very safe pilot. It also turned out that she had summited and guided to the top of Denali 7 times. We took off with clear weather reported from base camp (it was overcast when we departed). Leighanne found a route that took us far to the west but assured us that we would be refunded our money if she could not get us up into the mountain.
The mountain was clear from the south western approach and the views were spectacular from both sides of the plane. Flew over Denali base camp and then Leighanne spotted an opening to land on Pika (?) glacier.
Spent 20 minutes on glacier and then returned. Very smooth flying with no airsickness for anyone.
Top compliments to TAT and to Leighanne - super enthusiastic, poised, confident and very knowledgeable.
This was our number one event of our 29 days in Alaska.

Review Text:
I highly recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi! Friends and I recently completed a Denali Climbing expedition, and I highly recommend TAT for your expedition needs. They cater to the climbers during the climbing season, with a focus on getting you onto and off of the glacier in a timely fashion. Their Basecamp personnel welcome the plane, and make getting fuel and getting going easy. She also did an outstanding job of coordinating basecamp departure, allowing us to keep our tent up as long as possible, while giving us plenty of warning before our flight out to get the tent down and get our gear assembled. The pilots were outstanding, efficient, yet friendly and informative.

During our "Talkeetna Hang" (waiting for flying weather), the staff at TAT was helpful, friendly and accommodating. They willingly gave us rides to/from Talkeetna, they let us have coffee, relax in/around the office, and happily explained what was happening with the glacier weather. Tom was exceptionally helpful in getting our gear weighed and prepped for the flight as well as giving/arranging rides to/from Talkeetna when we needed them.

Also, having the bunk-house for climbers was fantastic. You never know when you are going to get stuck doing the Talkeetna Hang, and having a place to crash was great (not 5 star accommodations, but for a climber it was great).

Although I didn't participate in a tourist flight, hanging around TAT, I observed that they take great pride in making sure that their flight-seeing tours are excellent, everyone getting on and off the planes had smiles on their faces, and while we were hanging around bugging the office staff, they continued to efficiently go about taking reservations and seeing to the needs of their flight-seeing customers.

Talkeetna Air Taxi is awesome!

Review Text: It was our last day in Talkeetna and we were surprised to see clear weather. When we checked out Denali Overlook Inn, the owner suggested we check out flightseeing as it was a good day for flying. He gave us $25 discount vouchers to Talkeetna Air. We called around 930am and they booked us for a 1 pm flight. Check in was easy and fast. Pilot gave us a brief instruction on safety and expectations and off we went. Flight was smooth going to the Alaskan range. Pilot gave us info while we went around the vast range of snow, glaciers and rock. It was a sight to behold! My sister actually said that it's overwhelmingly beautiful that no amount of photos can capture the grandeur of the mountain ranges. We were able to see Mt Denali's peak; the pilot did turns so both sides of the plane can take in the sight. Overall it took about an hour of flying. We felt safe and enjoyed it immensely. Many times, people we met tell us only a percentage of tourists see Denali's peak when they visit because of the weather; so if you have chance to see it, grab that opportunity!

Review Title: weather didn't cooperate but company was A+
Review Text: We booked the flightseeing around Denali with glacier landing. Unfortunately for us, we had excellent weather for the entire trip except the afternoon we planned to do this excursion. It had been cloudy and a little rainy earlier but when we checked in to fly it was improving. We were told that the mountains were clear but there was a lot of clouds in the valley between us and the mountains. We were given the option of trying to find a way through the clouds but were warned that a glacier landing probably wouldn't happen unless conditions improved before we got there. Otherwise we could cancel or reschedule. Since we had to leave early in the morning and couldn't reschedule, we decided to try. Our pilot was Alex and he tried to break through the clouds in 3 different places, but ultimately we had to turn back. I was very disappointed that it didn't work out but was very impressed with the professionalism and commitment on the part of TAT to both keep us safe and accommodate us. In the end, they refunded the deposit which I wasn't expecting. Definitely give these guys your business if you plan to see Denali by air!

Review Text:
I used this company fifteen years ago for a Mount McKinley flight and they were wonderful. So, I decided to use them again. I phoned them to make the reservation, and they were very helpful. We were going in to Talkeetna by train and I was concerned about the time frame. After securing the date and time I immediately received an email with details and instructions. They offered to pick us up at the station; I declined because I thought we would have plenty of time to explore the town and walk to the terminal.
