Review Text: During our drive from Anchorage to Denali, we stopped in Talkeetna for our 11 am reserved flight.  It was cloudy out and I assumed that flights would be canceled, but I was wrong and they said visibility at Denali was excellent.  So we loaded on the 10 passenger plane and next thing I knew we were in the air.  We flew under the clouds for about 20 minutes then followed a glacier upwards.  We flew right through a hole in the clouds and the landscape changed dramatically.  In front of us were rugged mountains covered in snow and ice.  The clouds were beneath us and the skies were crystal blue.  We flew right up to the side of Denali and the pilot made some leisurely turns so that both sides of the plane could see everything around us.  Then the pilot said we would be landing and the next thing I knew we were touching down on a flat snow covered plain (glacier) in the middle of soaring mountain peaks.  My family and I stepped out of the plane into a winter wonderland with approximately 2 feet of fresh snow.  We took in the sights and took pictures for the next 20 or so minutes.  We witnessed a small avalanche on one of the mountains nearby.  We all got back on the plane, took off, and headed back to Talkeetna. The whole experience was about 1 hour and 45 minutes.  The flying was perfectly smooth the whole time. We did the Mountain Voyager With Landing.  My adult daughter-in-law said it was the most amazing experience of her life (she hasn't had children yet!). It's expensive but if you can afford it, an experience worth doing once in your life. Tip - the pilot may offer the front seat (next to pilot) to anyone who is interested.  On the way up one of the other passengers rode up front.  I asked to switch positions with him on the way down and he agreed.  Might be better on way down as I was kind of distracted watching the pilot do his thing. The plane windows are quite large and all my pictures came out really clearly with no reflection.

Review Text:
We drove from Anchorage to Denali, and the weather was perfect: Blue sky, barely any clouds, Denali easily visible from the road. So, we spontaneously stopped in Talkeetna and booked a flight-seeing tour and boy was that a good decision!
I hadn't booked a flight-seeing tour in advance because all research indicated that the weather is unpredictable. So, we were extremely lucky!

The little airport is easily found, it's not like Talkeetna is that big :-)
They weigh you in and you can even leave your purse with the staff, if you don't want to leave it in the car.
They give you glacier shoes, and then you go up in a propeller plane (a Cessna in my case) and have stunning views of Denali National Park!
Remember, there is really only one road, Parks Hwy. And there is only one road in the park, and it's not very long.
From the air you begin to realize the vastness of the place! You see the tree line, little lakes with cabins and no roads leading to them. You see glaciers and where glaciers used to be (hello, global warming). You see the pure granite mountains and snow and glacier ponds and so so much more!

We landed on Ruth Glacier and it was so beautiful. Quiet. Pristine untouched slow, clear blue sky, the freshest air you can imagine. Just ... peaceful.

It was an amazing experience worth every penny. If you can afford it and if it seems right, do it! You won't regret it!

We had a very small window of clear weather, and we hit it perfectly, allowing the light to play on the mountain faces so uniquely and extravagantly. Our pilot was full of knowledge and very enjoyable to talk with. He took us within what felt like arms length from the mountain sides multiple times, and we circled in and out of various pockets of clear space surrounded on all sides by vertical walls of granite and ice. The experience was truly one of a kind, and I couldn't have asked for a better journey to glorious Mt. Denali. Thank you so much Talkeetna Air Taxi!

Review Text: If you get the opportunity to do this, don't miss it. The scenery is unreal - it has to be seen. We went for it and didn't regret it at all. We appreciated the advice of the experienced team at Talkeetna Air Taxi - you could feel they really love what they are doing and are not there to make a quick buck. So if you are in Talkeetna or on the way to Denali - definitely make a stop here for couple of hours and make sure you see the highest mountain in North America. By the way, we only saw the top of Denali from the Talkeetna Air Taxi plane - for the three days we spent at Denali, the mountain was nowhere to be seen :).

Let me just say that although I had MANY stellar photos from Alaska, the view of the snow-covered mountains taken from the window of this small airplane -- with my iPhone -- became the cover photo for my Alaska photo album! Words cannot describe the breath-taking beauty from the air above Mt. McKinley. The excursion we purchased also included a glacier landing, but we were fortunate enough to actually land at the base camp for climbers to pick up a lone climber finishing up his trek, which was fascinating in itself.

There really are no words to describe this adventure, and the staff and pilots from Talkeetna Air Taxi were no less exceptional. If there's any way you can afford the money for this adventure, I HIGHLY recommend you spend it here!

Review Text:
It's hard to not sound overly-enthusiastic about the glacier-landing trip my wife and I took with Talkeetna Air Taxi but it was nothing short of astounding. Our guide recommended this outfit and they did not disappoint.
The weather had cleared as we were driving into Talkeetna and the full mountain range was free of clouds and brightly lit against a blue sky. We had been scheduled for a trip the following day but T.A.T. rearranged our schedule to accommodate us while the weather was at a peak for flying. They were busy because of the optimal weather and we had a brief wait during which we were outfitted with ice booties (?) and watched the planes buzzing in and out of the airstrip.
Our pilot was very friendly and informative, pointing out major sights along the way to the glacier and answering questions. The time on the glacier itself was magical and the place seemed almost fake because of the scale, grandeur and beauty of the stone and ice against the blue sky. We were even fortunate enough to witness an avalanche a few minutes after landing - something I understand to be unusual on a large scale.
There are multiple air taxi companies that make this trip and I can't speak to the experiences that any of the others offer, but I can say that our visit with T.A.T. was nothing short of excellent.

Review Title: One of the most amazing taxi rides you can take. Once in lifetime! Amazing!
Review Text: We took the talkeetna air taxi adventure to about 14,000 feet on one of the largest glaciers in the world deeper then the Grand Canyon well over made wide. We landed at the base camp and had the opportunity to get out wonder around in very fresh snow on the glacier. Their were many hikers staying at the base camp getting used to the altitude and practice hiking so they could hike to the next camp level. On this particular day we crossed paths with the first small group to reach the summit of Denali and return back to take the taxi down. I have done 3 of the most amazing adventures in Alaska. The plane ride up with the plane driver talking to us about the different glaciers and how high we were going was exciting and amazing. I hope I get one more time to go up and wonder around perhaps stay over night on the glacier it was incredible and I wish everyone could take this trip once. It changes the way you think when you realize how big that glacier is 45 miles long, deeper then Grand Canyon and at least mile or more wide. Hiker look like ants on the glacier from the small plane. Adventure of a life time.

Review Title: On a clear day, you can see forever!
Review Text:
We were blessed with good weather for our flight around Denali. We really appreciate the professionalism that Telkeetna Air extended to us for our flight. We had booked a "Grand" tour of Denali, but the weather was not favorable to see anything. The office staff was very easy to work with offering a lesser flight, a full refund, or they would get us out on the "Grand" tour the next day. Mother Nature was not about to give us a break, and we went through the same scenario the next night with us receiving a full refund. We were departing the next day, but when I went to bed at midnight, (the sun never sets in June, I had no idea it was that late) I realized that the clouds had lifted, and after driving up to the lookout point to catch a glimpse of The Great One, Denali. I contacted Talkeetna Air first thing that morning, and they got us out on one of the most amazing flight tours we have ever experienced. We requested a late checkout, at the RV park we were staying at, and were able to make our destination that evening.

On a clear day, you can see forever! We had a clear day, and Denali is something that you really need to be up close to really grasp the majestic magnitude of the mountain. The Great One is very appropriate. Landing on a glacier was really the icing on the cake, for the flight.

Thank you Talkeetna Air, you really helped make our trip to Alaska, the "Trip of A Lifetime".

The staff was very friendly, knowledgeable, and professional. The plane was clean, and comfortable to be in. The pilot was very informative with stories about Denali, and kept you glued (okay, I did have my seatbelt on) to my seat with the shear beauty of the mountains surrounding Denali.

Review Text:
The absolute highlight of this year's trip to Alaska was our flight among the mountains of Denali and the glacier landing. Clouds over "the great one" prevented a clear view of Denali the day of our flight. This disappointment was offset by the incredible beauty of the surrounding mountains and glaciers. ( You should know that clouds obscure part or all of Denali more than half the time. So plan accordingly. ). The glacier landing was a thrill of a lifetime. Walking about on a thousands feet deep sheet of snow and ice was mind bending and the views were spectacular. I used up the batteries on two cameras before we landed back at Talkeetna.

I have never felt safer on a plane of any size ( 7 seats in this case ) than I did on this flight, despite flying through narrow passes with towering granite peaks on each side. Our pilot was friendly, professional, experienced and highly skilled. He narrated the entire flight with interesting information and described the technical aspects of the flight ( flying through passes, glacier landing, etc ) in a way that was both fascinating and reassuring. Despite the planes small size, the flight was smoother and more stable than most commercial airline flights. It was as solid as sitting on your living room sofa.

The staff at Talkeetna Air were extremely courteous and helpful. From the reservation process to pre-flight orientation to post flight, they could not have been nicer. I would definitely do this again and I would highly recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi.

Review Title: Don't go if it's cloudy. Read other 'poor/average' for similar comments.
Review Text:
This activity was a huge let down after reading the glowing reviews on here and numerous travel books stating this as a 'must-do' activity. Then again not all must-do activities I've experienced were all great either.

Weather plays a HUGE role in the type of experience you will get. Not only does it dictate what you see, but also your mood as well (we all love that blue sky). We had originally booked the Grand Denali tour but due to the cloudy weather it was cancelled and was rescheduled for the Mountain Voyager tour (that should have been my cue to bail with this activity!

You do get some great views from the plane but it does fly quite high and the window is not super big. We did see Mount Denali and some other mountains but only partial views due to clouds, which I understand is typical for high mountains. But it was cloudy all over and the light level wasn't the best for taking photos. We also landed on a glacier but there were several other planes and people all around taking photos. It was hard to enjoy the surroundings with people talking and asking you to take their photo. Because of the cloud cover on the glacier we had limited views of our surroundings as well.

I would NOT recommend this activity if it's cloudy. Think about the amount of money you pay. I do recommend going on a helicopter tour instead. I did that in Valdez and WOW that was so much better. You have much better views and you fly very close to the mountains and glaciers. We also did a glacier landing and had glacier water. In my opinion going via helicopter was a much better experience than going on an airplane. And besides we've all been on planes but being in a helicopter was an amazing experience.

Save your money and do a helicopter landing instead!

Review Title: Unforgettable Flight Tour of “The Great One!”
Review Text:
My husband and I recently took a Grand Denali with Glacier Landing flight tour with Talkeetna Air. You must add this flight tour to the top of your bucket list. It was without a doubt, the most incredible flight tour we have ever taken! Our pilot Richard provided us with a wonderfully smooth flight, gave excellent narrative and pointed out areas of interest and landed us right on Ruth Glacier. What an adrenaline rush!

This was the priciest tour we booked for our Alaska vacation, and it was worth every cent and then some. Some experiences are just so incredible, they leave a lifetime impression. This was one of those experiences. A flight tour of Denali gives you a taste of the sheer enormity of the mountain and the surrounding peaks. Majestic, staggering, astonishing, stunning, breathtaking…I think you get the idea! Words fall short in trying to describe the magnificent scenery. Denali is the highest mountain peak in North America, and we flew by the Wickersham Wall, which is the highest vertical drop in the world, even higher than Everest. No wonder Denali translates as “The Great One!”

Take our advice, if you do a Denali flight tour, spend the extra money and do a glacial landing. It will blow you away! It gives you an idea of what the mountain climbers see and feel. We were 5500 feet up and it was a gorgeous sunny day. It didn’t even feel very cold. They give you boots to place over your shoes, and some layered fleece works just fine. Just imagine throwing Denali snowballs at each other! We were very fortunate to have unusually clear weather. This is a flight tour that sometimes gets cancelled due to weather, so try and book it early in your trip to leave room to reschedule. That’s why you only put down a small deposit, with the majority due on the flight day. And if you’ve heard of the “30% Club,” which is the percentage of Alaska travelers who actually see Denali, taking a flight tour increases your chances you’ll see it.

We chose to fly out of Talkeetna because it is the closest distance to the mountain. The majority of your flight is spent viewing Denali, rather than flying to it. That’s why a flight out of Denali National Park or Anchorage costs more than from Talkeetna, since more of the flight time is spent just getting there. You also will not find a helicopter glacial landing tour for Denali, only flight planes. The only reason there aren’t helicopter landings on Denali is because the tour companies that are currently operating these flights were grandfathered in when Denali was made a National Park, and were only doing plane landings. That’s also why there are a limited number of companies that have permits to do a Denali glacier landing. Some claim to have a Denali helicopter landing, but look closely and you will see it lands elsewhere, not on Denali. If you’re going to spend that kind of money, make sure you see the real McCoy!

We chose Talkeetna Air for its superb safety record and quality pilots. Richard, our pilot was a wealth of interesting facts and stories. As he tells it, doing these flight tours never get old. He enjoys every minute and it shows in his enthusiasm! Booking with Talkeetna Air was a breeze, and they even offered a senior discount. Everyone was very friendly, efficient and helpful. Their pricing is competitive, and their service is outstanding.

If you are going to tour Alaska, a flight tour of Denali with a glacier landing should be placed at the top of your excursion list. Book with the folks who do it best, Talkeetna Air, and marvel at the experience of a lifetime!

Review Text:
I called the company directly and booked a flight for the same day. I had not done it in advance because the weather in the area can be very fickle.
Everyone I talked to or had any interaction with at Talkeetna Air Taxi was very courteous and accommodating, very willing to answer all my questions.
They even had someone pick me up from the Princess shuttle drop-off bus lot in Talkeetna, and return me there after my flight, even though I was the only person who needed that service. Their office and airstrip are a nice little hike outside town.
Once at their office, it was a very simple, efficient process of getting checked in and getting “glacier boots”, even though I had not booked a flight that included a glacier landing.
Our pilot, Tom Falley, a consummate pro with a sense of humor, explained all the safety procedures we needed to know prior to boarding, and before gently helping us climb in.
Once aloft, is was one continuous experience of jaw dropping, spectacular scenery, from the braided rivers, plains, and foothills to the drama of glaciers, and rocky spires that reached to the sky, sometimes disappearing in clouds, and the occasional soft streak of sunshine on an alpine snow field, or a serene glacial lake.
Throughout the flight, pilot Falley enriched his passengers with pertinent facts and anecdotes about what lay below us, and sometimes remained silent, allowing us to appreciate it all in our own souls.
It did not surprise me to learn later from the company website that our pilot, Tom Falley, in addition to his impressive set of piloting skills and experience, has a Masters in geology. I certainly learned a lot from him on my flight. Who knew that algae grow on glaciers, and their effect on those glaciers and on global climate changes? Thanks, Tom.
Thanks also for your obvious commitment to safety. I think we might have gotten some extra flight time as pilot Falley tried every safe way he could to get us to a higher elevation to see more, but ultimately, the clouds and safety won out.
I would strongly recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi to anyone looking for a superlative experience.

Review Text:
The biggest piece of advice I can offer is to try to be flexible with trying to do a flight seeing tour of Denali. The weather around the mountains is just about impossible to predict and heavy cloud cover around the mountains is common.

This is our second tour with TAT. We flew with them about 16 years ago when it was just my wife and I. This time it was a three generation group of six of us. We had planned to to the "Grand Denali" tour and had it booked for our first full day in Talkeetna. However, the clouds were not cooperating that day and they had actually not gone up for any flights. Over the course of the next couple of days, we rescheduled a few times and juggled some of the other activities that we had planned. Finally, on our last morning before heading to Anchorage to fly home, the weather cleared enough to allow a flying tour of the glaciers and lower peaks. Denali itself was initially not visible, but we dressed for the potential for the glacier.

The tour itself was excellent. Our pilot/guide was very familiar with the area, the landmarks on the ground, and the geological characteristics of the area we toured. His communication to us was excellent, and I was even more impressed with his communication with the other flights operating. Ours was the first flight of the morning, so he was also acting as a scout to pass back to others how conditions were looking.

He made several looks at potential glacier landing spots, but all were too cloudy to bother with. Finally, near the end of our time, the glacier area that serves as base camp for those who set out to climb Denali was clear. We were able to make the glacier landing. Mt. Foraker had the best visibility and we took most of our group pictures in front of it. However, the peak of Denali was also visible for a while during our stop and we got to appreciate just how big of a rock it is from about 15 miles from the peak. Our pilot took lots of great pictures with our phones and my camera of our group and helped make an incredible memory that we will all carry forever.

I highly recommend flying with these folks.

Review Text:
I was extremely nervous for this once-in-a-lifetime activity. I felt sick the entire drive from Anchorage to Talkeetna just thinking about it, as I had never been on a small plane before and was extremely worried. When we arrived at the office, we asked if they had any recommendations on what to wear in terms of layers, hats/gloves, etc and they were not very helpful. The person working the desk just looked up on the board what the temperature was but did not have advice on how to dress appropriately for the glacier landing.

We ended up leaving ahead of schedule because everyone was there (which included myself and husband, another party of 2, and 3 hikers). My husband told the pilot how nervous I was and if he had any words of advice to help calm me down. He didn't say anything particularly helpful (such as later in the day when he told us he's been flying that route daily for about 20 years, which is what I would've wanted to hear!).

The day in Talkeetna was cloudy and gray and it made me nervous going through the clouds. It was reassuring to be wearing the headset and hearing the pilot communicating with other pilots. Once we got above the clouds, it was sunny and we had much clearer views of Denali and the other mountains. The pilot did a good job pointing out the summits and adding facts.

Our glacier landing was at "base camp" which is 7000 ft up and where hikers congregate before beginning or after ending their hike up Denali. The landing on the glacier was pretty smooth. Being on the glacier was one of the coolest parts and I would recommend it if it can fit into your schedule and budget. It was also pretty neat to see the hikers and hear some of their stories.

The flight back to the office was pretty similar to the way there - full of incredible, breathtaking views. When we got back it was a little disorganized. We went to say thank you but the pilot was busy with the plane and no one from the office greeted us back. We went into the office after a couple of minutes and they gave us a few postcards. I kind of expected them to be more upbeat and ask how our flight was, etc.

Overall, I am glad we did it. The experience did feel more like the "taxi" service part of their name than the welcoming, small-town tourist experience I was imagining. We got to and from the glacier safely, which was my main concern, and saw some amazing views.

A Talkeetna Air shuttle van met our bus and took us to the airport. After the flight, the Talkeetna shuttle was willing to drive us wherever we wanted, but we walked to the town.
Checkin at the airport was flawless, plenty of friendly staff who knew what they were doing.

As for the flight-- My wife and I were seated on opposite sides of the plane. The pilot did a great job of circling around so that both sides could see everything. My wife's face was plastered to the window... she didn't move except to turnaround quickly a few times and order me to "take a picture." It just so happened that every time she looked, I had put the camera down. I was worried that I was taking TOO MANY! Every shot was like a post card.

I should note that the peak was not visible from the ground. This flight allowed us to see the majesty of the mountain range and peaks above the clouds.

It got even better when we landed on the snow! After we landed the pilot showed us how he can convert from wheels to skis.

My only complaint was that it didn't last long enough!!!

We flew in helicopters and sea planes while in Alaska... this was the tops.

A must do.

Review Title: The Glacier Landing is a Must!
Review Text: I started planning for our trip months in advance and was able to find a discount on their website.  I was nervous about booking so far in advance, but it turned out great. The people that work there are very patient and want you to have the best trip.  We were scheduled to go up in the early evening on a cloudy, somewhat rainy day.  We were able to talk to people who had just come back and see some of their photos.  We decided to take a chance and re-book for a few days later and see if we could get better weather.  It was a gamble, but it paid off.  The best part, they still charged us the same rate as if we had gone at our originally scheduled time.  This is a very expensive activity, but I'm glad we decided to do it...it was thrilling!  We had better weather the day we flew and Denali was out for a bit.  I was able to sit in the seat next to the door, which was great for taking pictures.  At first, I panicked because everything our pilot was narrating was on the other side of the plane, but he started turning the plane so that both sides got a turn to see what he was talking about.  The closer we got to the glacier and into the mountains, the bumpier the ride got.  We hit one air pocket that made everyone gasp.  I won't lie, it scared us a little!  But, our pilot was calm and navigated to smoother air.  We were able to land on a glacier and that was just awesome!  The views from the air are spectacular, but I cannot imagine doing this trip without the glacier landing.  Dress in layers, as it was actually pretty warm on the glacier (it was chilly in the plane, or I thought so sitting next to the door...it was a little drafty in that seat!).  If you don't have boots, they give you slip on booties to keep your shoes dry.  The only thing I would have wished for is a pilot with a little more interaction...he was probably our least favorite "guide" on our trip, but he got us there and back in one piece and that is the most important thing!  Definitely recommend this activity and see if you can find discounts if you are worried about the price.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
I thought this would be a fun activity, but it was so much better than expected. Before boarding the 9-passenger plan, we were outfitted with glacier boots. It was an overcast day and the first 10 minutes were fairly unremarkable. Then we got above the cloud cover and within minutes we were flying between and above mountain peaks with breathtaking views of the glaciers below. It was a bit of a rush because at times we flew very close to the mountains, which added to the excitement, but nothing compared to experience of landing on a glacier.
When we exited the plane, it was as if we were on another planet. The silence alone was an awesome experience. We had the opportunity to walk around and our party engaged in a snowball fight. Just standing on the glacier so high up was unbelievable, but the actual landing and takeoff was a bit of an adrenaline rush.
During the flight passengers wear head phones because it's really loud up there, and this is the only way you can hear the pilot. I believe there are less expensive trips available that don't include a glacier landing, but this is not the place to be frugal. Definitely do the glacier landing because you'll never forget get. It truly is an experience of a lifetime.

Review Title: Stunning views, amazing flight and glacier landing!
Review Text:
We had high hopes for this flight and they were met superbly. Check-in was well organised. We were asked if we could come in for a slightly earlier flight than booked on the day which was fine. Shoes were provided to give extra grip on the glacier. There was 8 passengers which filled up the plane and there were a few flights going at similar times. The flight was amazing, particularly as we got to the snow covered mountains. The wing perhaps slightly obstructs the view but not much, it was great. The pilot also gave us a little information about what we were passing by. I was spellbound by the scenery. It was a beautiful, cloudless day though the pilot did say that it is only that clear about 20% of days. Not long before landing there was some currents making it a bit bumpy so I think the 1 and a quarter hour return flight plus 30 minutes at the glacier was plenty. Landing on the snow covered glacier and getting out for a little walk near the plane was fun, and we enjoyed seeing other planes flying in and out. If you just take the bus trip through Denali (which is still good) you will not get views to match this.
I believe this company in Talkeetna is also slightly cheaper than getting a flight tour from Denali. Recommended!

Review Title: The Most Incredible Activity I've Ever Experienced!
Review Text:
BLOWN AWAY!

This was probably the coolest thing I have every done in my life. I can't thank Talkeetna Air Taxi enough.

The people in the office were such a big help in the booking process. Not only was getting all of the information I needed for the flight a breeze, they were also extremely helpful and forthcoming with information. While awaiting my flight, I heard other customers asking all sorts of questions... some relating to the flight, others just about Alaska in general. This being my first time in Alaska, I soaked all of this information in like a sponge and before I even boarded the plane I had already learned a lot about the Alaskan range.

Next was the flight. My pilot was Jonathan and he made me feel extremely informed and safe before boarding. I like to consider myself quite the outdoors-man/thrill seeker, but I had never been in a small plane before, nor one going into one of the tallest mountain ranges out there. I felt at ease and completely safe during my flight. Not only were the views literally INDESCRIBABLY incredible, but Jonathan narrated the whole flight. I was like a sponge again, gaining so much fascinating information about the Alaskan range and the area in general.

The weather was perfect for our flight so Jonathan informed us that we would be making the Glacier landing. I never have my heart race so much before. Before I knew it, we landed smoothly in the fresh powder and I was standing on a glacier on Denali. There have been few things I've experienced in my life that literally took my breath away. You can never truly understand how small you are until you are standing with these mountains towering around you.

While on the glacier Jonathan was quick to answer any questions about the glacier or anything relating to Alaska. He also took some pictures of me and my friend while on the glacier. One thing that I'd like to point out about this is as a hobby, I really enjoy photography. I can really appreciate when someone using my camera can frame and focus my camera correctly. Jonathan took some great pictures of both me and my friend. It's pretty cool when you pilot also is a great photographer, --bonus points there.

After our time on the glacier we finally got back to Talkeetna, and I was able to drool over all of the pictures I was able to take on this trip. This was truly one of greatest experiences of my life and I highly recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi. Not only did they safely land me on a glacier in one of the most awe-inspiring places in the world, but the whole time they were always there to answer any questions I had. From the pilot to the office staff, everyone seemed to click like one big family. I plan to go back to Alaska with my wife next year, and I am totally doing this flight again with her!

5 Stars!

Review Title: READ THIS REVIEW BEFORE PLANNING YOUR TRIP!!!
Review Text:
I had always thought these trips were too expensive, and probably not worth it - thus passing on several opportunities. This trip we went ahead and booked one, and then tried over several days to actually make the trip, as the weather was preventing flying - pushing the trip back further and further. We almost cancelled rather than drive two hours (one way) to make a final attempt, but things looked good - so we went for it, and got in the air.

Once in a lifetime is an over-used phrase. In this case, it is absolutely spot on! I won't spoil it by giving you details of things that can't adequately be described with words, and instead will give advice...

Weather can be particularly uncooperative for these trips, so it's best to schedule your overall trip to allow many attempts at getting in the air. The staff is amazingly capable and willing to work with you to get you into the air when you can, but you want to give them lots of chances if your scheduled attempt fails.

Make sure your camera and phone batteries are charged.

Layer your clothing so that you can be wrapped up like the kid in A Christmas Story, or shirtless like the crazy kid on our trip. You can never be sure what will be best.

Wear waterproof shoes, but they don't need to be perfect. They have shoe covers if you need them. Bring good sunglasses.

Pee before you get on the plane

Be prepared to spend time in Talkeetna waiting for your flight if the weather is bad. There's lots to see and do.

It was an unforgettable vacation, and a definite high point was our Grand Denali w/ glacier landing trip with Talkeetna Air Taxi. The weather wasn't cooperating the day that we originally booked our trip for, but Talkeetna Air Taxi was very accomodating and rebooked us for another day that fit in our very busy itinerary (and we're very grateful that they did). The views of the mountains, glacial rivers and the up close and personal view of the glacier that we landed on was an absolutely incredible experience.

We highly recommend this Alaskan adventure!

Review Title: Expensive trip, good view, bad weather

The pilot was knowledgeable, the flight there was pleasant, and we saw many great views. Around McKinley, however, it was very cloudy. We can see it up close, but a bit further, a lot of the views were blocked, which was very disappointing.

We had a glacier landing, where we got off the plane, wandered around in the snow, and took many awesome pictures for 20-30 minutes. One visitor is designated the copilot on the way there, sitting next to the pilot up front. After the stopping point, another visitor got a chance to be copilot, so that part was fun. Coming back, the views are pretty much the same.

Overall, we paid $300-400 per person for the flight. Did we see great things? Yes, it was fantastic. Was it worth $400? I'm not too sure. Maybe if the weather was better...I appreciate Talkeetna Air Taxi's policy of a full refund if the weather was bad, but I think we caught the worst weather that's still flyable, so it was still a good experience, but for that price, I wish it was better.

Review Title: Most of it has been said already, but...
Review Text:
to put my two cents worth in, this is a large, very professional sky-bus (large 10-passenger aircraft) tour operator that specializes in providing tourists a close up and personal look at America's most famous mountain.
The staff works hard to accommodate the constant flow of tourists, and cope with the ever-changing weather conditions the mountain creates... which plays havoc with any kind of regularly scheduled flights.
We ended up taking the 900 HP IFR-rated turbine Otter up the Ruth Glacier, and after an extensive flight to view the Mountain from every possible angle, out pilot Richard skillfully maneuvered the big bird into the Don Sheldon Ampitheater of the glacier for a short and soft landing. We were able to get out and enjoy a brief walkaround, throw a few snowballs and admire the scenery before jumping back aboard for the flight down through the mouth of the glacier and back to Talkeetna.
This was a great highlight of our trip, and should be on the 'bucket list' of anyone planning a trip to Alaska. The IFR capability translates to a better chance of getting you up to the mountain when the weather at lower altitudes is cloudy, and that proved to be a real plus.

Review Text:
My wife and I took a flight-seeing tour with Talkeetna Air Taxi to see Mt. McKinley (Denali) and chose to do the glacier landing as well. Our pilot Dave answered all our questions, kept us informed of what we were seeing, and really made it a very enjoyable time for us. He made sure to swing the plane around points of interest on both sides for long enough for everyone to get a great view. We love seeing the unique things about the places we travel, and Denali and Alaska's many glaciers definitely qualify as unique!

To me the best thing about this trip was actually the biggest challenge. TAT makes it very clear if the weather is not ideal for viewing the mountain, you can back out with no issues. But for me, I didn't have another day to wait for perfect conditions! So barring total cloud cover, we were going on the trip. We got a warm greeting at the office, some helpful instruction and safety info from our pilot Dave, and he let my wife ride co-pilot and take in the amazing views. We could see some clouds around the mountain, but Dave was in constant communication with the other TAT pilots about what they were seeing and the best places to get the best views. So even though people say sometimes it's hard to even see the mountain with the fickle weather, we got amazing views, incredible pictures and just a wonderful experience. Thanks to Dave and all his colleagues for doing things right - understanding that sharing their information was going to make sightseeing better for everyone.

The whole team at TA is first-rate. Can't say enough good things. There is no better way to see Denali, and I highly recommend the glacier landing. I doubt I will ever experience anything quite like it. Thanks again to Dave for taking us on a truly memorable trip and hopefully we'll be back again soon to do it again!

Review Text:
The people at Talkeetna Air Taxi were very accommodating and personable from the moment we made arrangements. We were on the land portion of cruise/land vacation with Princess and didn't know the logistics of getting to the town of Talkeetna from the lodge. They were very understanding and made sure we understood that it would take an hour plus to get there and they would have someone waiting for us to get us to the plane for our glacier landing.
We arrived at Talkeetna a little late due to road work on the only road to get there, were met at the bus from the lodge and were reassured that the plane wouldn't leave without us. The 10 passenger plane waited for our late arrival and off we went.
The day was crystal clear and the pilot gave a steady stream of interesting information as we flew over mountains, glaciers and rock formations. Everyone was taking pictures and the views were mesmerizing. About 20 minutes later, we were landing on the glacier and couldn't believe what we were looking at. The views were breathtaking, the temperature was actually warm with the sun radiating off the snow and it is true - we only needed a small jacket. In fact, that day, short sleeves were almost comfortable. They gave us boots to go over our shoes so the soft snow wasn't a problem and we could walk around admiring the views.
Although the ride isn't cheap, we thought this excursion was the best one of our trip. To think, we viewed Mt McKinley/Denali from a distance several times during our trip and admired it's beauty and now we were actually on it! We followed Ruth Glacier on the ride back with a great commentary.
We would recommend the glacier landing and particularly Talkeetna Air Taxi due to their professionalism and very personable people both while making arrangements before our trip and when we arrived at their desk.
(BTW -while in Talkeetna, you have to have lunch at the "Spinach Bread" food truck on main street.)

Review Title: Amazing experience of Denali and Ruth Glacier
Review Text:
My boyfriend and I took the $350 Base Camp Tour with Glacier Landing flightseeing trip and it was worth every cent. We were very lucky to have clear weather and were in a plane with 10 passengers. We flew up to Denali and went around about 270 degrees and back, including over the Denali climbing base camp, which was really interesting. The pilot made sure to go back and forth so that everyone could take pictures, no matter what side of the plane they were on. We landed on Ruth Glacier and stayed for about 20 minutes, but couldn't go very far from the plane unfortunately. In the future, I would look into doing a longer trip with some trekking around the glacier. Nevertheless, it was beautiful and awe-inspiring. The scale of the mountains and glaciers is just unbelievable.

The only complaint I would have is about the smell of diesel in the plane. It wasn't overwhelming, but if you're sensitive to it, you wouldn't enjoy it very much.

Overall, it was an amazing trip that I would recommend to anyone. We didn't go up to Denali NP for the bus trip, so this was a great way to see it anyway. If you're staying in Talkeetna, or are active US military, ask about their discounts. We ended up saving over $100 total off the $700 bill.

Review Title: Worth Every Penny!  Don't Miss This!
Review Text:
Talkeetna was the last stop on our week long visit to Alaska, with a flightseeing trip being the main reason for the visit. We had reserved a flight in the afternoon of our last full day in Alaska but unfortunately the planes couldn't fly due to the weather. We were told to try back the following morning.

The next morning we went to breakfast at The Roadhouse (don't miss that if you come to Talkeetna!), and called Talkeetna Air Taxi at 8am when they opened to see if they'd be flying. They said things were clear so we should come asap! We were so happy!

We did the Mount McKinley trip with glacier landing. At check-in we signed waivers, got weighed (only the folks behind the desk see the results) and picked out some "boots" to put over our hiking shoes since there was snow on the glacier. The shoe covers are lightweight but they help keep the powdery snow out of your shoes so I'd recommend using them (they are free).

We had about 10 people on our plane. The pilot did a nice job of pointing out things as we were flying and was very personable. Everyone has a headset to wear so you can hear the pilot easily. We felt very safe the whole time.

There are no words that could do justice to this experience! We are people that live frugally and we really struggled with whether to pay so much for three of us to take this flight but it was worth every single penny! It was hands down the most incredible thing we did during our Alaska trip, so please don't hold back. You will not regret it!

The views of the mountain range are spectacular and give you a feel for the immensity of the range. It was breathtaking. The best part though, was the glacier landing. To land in two feet of powdery snow, see the tents of the folks who will be attempting to climb McKinley, look up at those vast mountains-it was the event of a lifetime. Truly. Yes, it costs more to land on the glacier, but that is what totally pushed the trip to being the highlight of our Alaska vacation.

We are SO happy that we took the Mt. McKinley flight and did the glacier landing. You will be too!

Review Text:
We did the McKinley Base Camp flight seeing tour with glacier landing (1 3/4 hours in total, and $350 each). It was totally worth every cent!

Check-in was very easy. They weigh each person, along with their backpacks, etc. but only the person behind the counter can see the weight. Then you put boots on over top of your shoes. There were five of us in the plane, plus our pilot Mike. We all had great window seats, and my friend got to sit in the co-pilot seat.

On our way to Mt McKinley we saw unbelievable beautiful scenery. But when we reached the mountain, it just took my breath away. Nobody asked many questions because our mouths were just open in awe. Mike was a fantastic pilot, and constantly turned left and right so that everyone sitting on both sides could get a great view of whatever he showed us.

We lucked out and had a beautiful blue sky sunny day, and could see the entire peak. Landing on the glacier was priceless. Everyone was so excited when we got out of the plane. It was like Christmas morning. It was actually quite warm up there, and very bright. Definitely take your sunglasses. We didn't need all the warm clothing we took with us. There were a few other planes on the glacier too, and people were throwing snow balls, and just enjoying the whole scene.

The flight back was just as beautiful, and Mike took us along a different route than on the way there. There was zero turbulence on the entire trip.

It was truly a highlight of the trip, and a once in a lifetime experience!

Review Title: Pricey - didn't live up to expectations
Review Text:
Unless the day is crystal clear, you will likely be disappointed in what you see. On the day we went, the sky was clear, so I was hopeful for some good photographs. However, by the time we got to the mountain (11:15am or so), the clouds had started to roll in and visibility was somewhat limited. The light was "flat" - so photo's were just so-so. If I had it to do over again, I'd book the first flight in the morning - the light would have been much better and perhaps much clearer views.

This outfit is well run - the planes seem in good shape and they operated safely. However, in the words of one of the other passengers - the trip was OK, but it wasn't great. My thinking exactly. If you decide to spend your money anyway, here are some tips:
1) Ask the pilot which side of the plane is best to sit on. The "other" side of the plane got most of the views, which was irritating as all get out to me.
2) One of the passengers on the plane was a bit heavy - 200 lbs? and had a bad knee. She was extremely uncomfortable and had to literally "unfold" herself to exit the plane. Seats are narrow and very limited leg room. You will also experience some bumpy air. I fly alot, so a non-issue for me - and it was brief - but you will likely experience a few bumps.
3) I thought we were going to land at base camp - we did not. We landed on a glacier somewhere in the area. You couldnt' see Mt McKinley from the landing, and photograph opportunities were pretty unremarkable. Save your money and bypass the glacier landing. You're basically just landing in the snow and walking around for a few minutes.
4) One of the women on our plane indicated that she had done this same flight 3 years ago, and had found it ho hum - and didn't find it much better the second time with her daughter. Again, it was OK - but not worth the $$$'s IMO.
The staff were nice and did not complain when I had to change the date of my visit to Talkeetna a couple of times - that was appreciated!
5) Our pilot had ear length, straight gray hair. He was okay - but wasn't great. He checked all the boxes is the best way to describe the experience.
6) Ask the pilot to "parallel" the peak so that you can see it. The pilot tended to fly headfirst towards the peak, so I'm sure he had a fabulous view of Mt. McKinley from his windshield. But passengers can only see out the side of the plane. So in essence, the only view you get of the peak is when he flies alongside the mountain. And you better be on the "right" side of the plane when he does. And the % of time you are viewing the actual peak will be very small - disappointingly so.

Review Title: Wow, A great suprise & wonderful time!
Review Text:

Upon arriving at Talkeetna Air, we checked in and were told to wait in their outside waiting area for our names to be called. We waited for over 15 minutes and finally one of the employees came to us (there were 4 of us in our party) and asked if we would mind sharing a plane that was going up and landing on the glacier instead of the flight we had booked. They would not charge us the difference. It would save them money to just add us to that flight than have to take another plane up for just our party. We said of course! I cannot say enough good about that flight and experience! After the fact, knowing now what we would have missed not landing on the glacier - I would highly recommend paying the extra to have that experience. It was outstanding and the flight would not have been nearly as enjoyable if we had just taken the plane up for sightseeing and not gotten to land, stop & walk around and experience stepping on the beauty of that mountain! It is hard to put into words how beautiful and exciting it is to land up there & get to step out & walk around (They supply snow boots that fit over your shoes so you can walk around up there). Our pilot was informative, gracious, and very helpful. Our flight could not have been better. It's a small plane, be prepared for a bumpy ride. It's a bit noisy but they supply earphones to buffer that, and you can hear the pilot narration.
This was definitely a highlight of our Alaskan vacation. Although we originally made the decision to save money by choosing the flight that did not land on the glacier, and got to experience it anyway, our advice is now to spend that extra money and experience the entire thing. It's a once in a lifetime adventure (for us anyway) and landing definitely made the entire excursion worth doing.
I would choose Talkeetna Air again; they were courteous, professional & made the entire experience one we will never forget!

We all had window seats and headphones and the pilot did a great job narrating.  You look back at the incredible photos you take and you confirm that this was just one of life's most exhilarating experiences.  Regarding cost, I suggest you keep checking their website for discounts.  I was debating whether to do the glacier landing in order to cut down on costs and was able to find a discount which basically made our glacier landing free.  I'm glad it was "free" because I felt this was the only part of the trip I could have skipped.  We landed on Ruth Glacier and while it was pretty and we got some great pictures, I felt it was underwhelming.  Because it's between the mountain peaks, I did not feel like I was "on top of the world" but only like we landed on snow.  So bottom line, do not miss this trip. Review Title: Talkeetna Air Taxi to Mt McKinley and Ruth Glazier
Review Text:
Go to be the highlight of our twelve day stay in Alaska. To see the beauty of Mt McKinley from the air was so much better than viewing it from the ground up. We had a wonderful time on our Southface Mt McKinley Flightsee that also included the optional landing on Ruth Glazier. The staff was very easy to work with to reserve our flight in advance a few weeks earlier. Can do this via internet or toll free 800 number.

The flight was very smooth on our six passenger plane plus the pilot. All of us received headphones so we could talk to and hear our pilot narrate our flight. We were fortunate to have a very clear day, not a cloud in the sky. After take off, we made the short flight to Mt Mckinley circle the south face and then headed for our smooth snow landing on Ruth Glacier. The total flight was just under two hours with one half hour of this walking around Ruth Glacier after we landed.

Talkeenta Air Taxi offers a 10% AAA discount and also will reduce the price $10 per person if you already have a National Park Pass ($10 one time cost for a lifetime pass if over age 62 from US National Park Service.)

As tours go this is a little pricing but if you came to Alaska to see it, pay them the money for a lifetime of great memories and photos. Would do it again in a heartbeat.

Before or after your flight be sure to spend some time in the town of Talkeetna. A great little town with several good restaurants and shops to explore. Town was the settling for old TV series, Northern Exposure. Still very nice place to visit and view Mt McKinley from a distance.

Review Text:
This was really difficult to rate. The experience itself (flying around Denali and landing on a glacier) is a full 5 star experience. If there was no other operator in Talkeetna, I would have rated this company higher, just based on how cool the experience is. (If you are wondering whether or not to splurge on a flight around Denali - do it, it's AMAZING). But this is a review of Talkeetna Air Taxi - the tour operator, not just a review of the scenic flight, and honestly, I wasn't that impressed with TAT.

After reading all the positive reviews, I chose to book with Talkeetna Air Taxi. I completed the online booking form and entered my credit card info. When I received my confirmation a few days later, I noted I had been scheduled for a different day than requested. Not the end of the world - I contacted the company, they apologized and rescheduled me for the correct day - but if I hadn't read my confirmation carefully, I'm sure it would been a much bigger deal to fix the day I was supposed to fly. Then about a week later, I received a voicemail letting me know they had needed to change the time of my flight - but the time they told me it was changed to was the time they had told me in the first place. Again, no big deal, but it did make me wonder how organized they were.

When my family arrived at the office on the day of our flight it was quite chaotic. People were landing and trying to buy t-shirts, people were checking in and needing to fill out forms and get weighed. When my turn to check in arrived, I asked how the weather was expected to be. I received a curt - "your flight will be fine" in response. I was asking, because we had planned to be in Talkeetna for a couple of days and had booked our flight right at the start so that we could postpone/reschedule if weather dictated. I got the feeling they were just too busy to talk to me.

Our flight was delayed by about 10 minutes, again - not a big deal, but we were waiting outside in the cold rain for those 10 minutes and no one from the company provided us with any information.

There was heavy cloud cover when we took off. During the first portion of our flight, the clouds completely enveloped the plane - nothing but white-out conditions outside my window. I have to tell you - I was nervous! Denali and the mountains around it stuck up out of the cloud cover and so the main portion of our flight was still amazing. The return was also completely clouded in. I do wish I had the opportunity to talk about the weather before the flight. Maybe they would have convinced me this was still the best chance, given how changeable the weather is, but since I never got to discuss it with them, I just don't know.

My other big complaint was that the pilot provided almost no commentary during the flight. He seemed a competent pilot, but he wasn't at all personable. There were many points during the flight where I really didn't know what I was looking at. I would have preferred an audio recording to the silence we mostly got. It also would have been nice for him to give a reassuring "don't worry about the clouds around Talkeetna, you'll see Denali just fine," during the first portion of the flight. I am particularly contrasting this experience to the wonder commentary provided by the pilot during my Misty Fjords scenic flight.

I know this review sounds fairly negative. I wasn't really that bad, I'm just balancing it against how much the trip cost and how many other operators there are that offer the same service. If you are anywhere near Talkeetna, you should definitely do a scenic flight around Denali and spend the extra to land on a glacier - it truly is an amazing experience. My experience with Talkeetna Air Taxi was perfectly adequate, but that's all.

Review Title: Grand Denali Air Tour with Talkeetna Air Taxi
Review Text:
Catching a perfect view of Denali / Mt. McKinley mountain is a roll of the dice, but who my sign up with for an aerial view can make a huge difference.
After checking with all the vendors that offer this service we (8 of us) went with Talkeetna Air Taxi (TAK) because they were the most flexible relative to us making the final decision on whether we go or don't go due the weather.
We were scheduled to fly at 11:15 on June 14th. We arrive only to find out there was a weather hold due to low clouds. So TAK moved us to a 4 PM flight. When we arrived for this flight and hear the comments from the vacationers that just got off the previous flight, were all very excited about the experience and sights they saw, so of course we said "lets go".
Once we got in the air, the clouds started to roll in. The pilot has a heck of a time finding holes in the clouds to work our way to the mountain. Once we got there, the clouds were so thick we probably saw only a bit of the mountain and we definitely couldn't land on the glacier due to the fog, so we headed back after a two hour flight.
When then disappointingly reported back to the office to settle up final payment, the front desk also felt our disappointment and before we said anything they offered to reduce our fare by near 60%, which was very generous.
in conclusion, if you are considering signing up for a flight over Denali, I would highly recommend contracting with Talkeetna Air Taxi.

The flight was smooth, the pilot was very professional and knowledgeable..it was all I could have ever asked for. He flew close to the mountain on all sides, so we could see more of the mountain than just it's south face. There are not enough adjectives to describe this mountain's grandeur or beauty!

Passengers are charged $10 each by the Park Service to land on the glacier, unless they have a senior national park pass or other park pass, which I had. Folks should give themselves the time to drive there from Anchorage or Fairbanks, and add time to have lunch or dinner in Talkeetna, a town with several excellent local restaurants (no national chains, thank goodness).

Review Text:
Talkeetna: Around the Denali
A few hours by car north of Anchorage towards the Mountain range lies the small Alaskan town of Talkeetna. A right turn from the main road will bring you to the airfield. There several companies offer sightseeing flights to and around the Mount McKinley (Denali). We selected the Talkeetna Air Taxi which operates a number of venerable Beavers and Otters besides a Cessna 182, all of them on skies. One can book several different routes. For us the tour around Mount McKinley with a landing on the glacier was the most appealing. On the flight to the mountains of the Alaska range the different colors of the tundra was beautiful to watch. We flew over many little lakes. The pilot acted also as tour guide and explained everything we could see. We followed a long glacier tongue crossed over a pass to come to the impressive north face of the Denali Mountain. Although we flew at about 10 000 feet we still remained well below the top of this snow covered giant of about 20 000 ft. A little further the pilot headed to a snow plateau where he put down the airplane softly on the snow covered glacier. We all stepped on the snow (it is advisable to wear firm shoes instead of sneakers) and enjoyed the sight of the surrounding 15 000 feet high mountains. Our pilot explained that we must not stay to long because the aircraft engine would cool down too much. Taking off downhill with the ground dropping away is always a great experience. The flight back to the airfield showed again the picturesque scenery of the tundra. This flight was definitely a highpoint of our Alaska trip. We highly can recommend it especially in the not so common case of picking a nearly cloudless day on both sides of the Alaskan range. One should add that there are many other activities to choose from, fishing, hiking kayaking to name just a few, while spending time in Talkeetna.
Ulrich Lanz, Munich Germany

Review Title: Beware of the importance of weather
Review Text: My trip was cancelled because the visibility was low. It was a valid reason. But I came to talkeetna only to do this activity. If not, I would have been in Fairbanks on that day watching aurora. TAT had cancelled all flights in the past two days. Weather was gloomy and drizzling for two days and weather prediction wasn't any different. TAT had my phone number and mail I'd. Still they didn't inform me until I reached their office. They were very sure that they wouldn't fly until the end of the day. If they had informed me earlier that they are so much dependent on weather, I would have made better plans for my limited time in Alaska. I understand that they cannot predict the weather completely and weather changes often. But they should let people know how much they are dependent on weather so that the customers can decide whether to risk their vacation time or not.

Review Text:
We tried to arrange a glacier landing while we were visiting Haily but the weather prevented us from flying there. So on our way back to Anchorage, we stopped by Talkeetna Air Taxi to see if they were doing glacier landings. They said that they were and that we should sign up for the 3:45 flight, which we did.

The other service that we tried to fly with wanted a credit card deposit and would not let us cancel in the event they were not doing glacier landings. Talkeetna Air Taxi, on the other hand, was very clear, if no glacier landing was possible before we took off, we could cancel with no penalty. That sealed the deal because the glacier landing was what we really wanted to do.

Our pilot, Tyler, was great. He gave commentary of the area during our flight and made us feel safe. The takeoffs and landings were smooth as silk.

I would highly recommend the glacier landing. It was well worth it.

Review Text: We stopped by Talkeetna on the way to Denali National Park and made reservation for flightseeing of Mt. McKinley and surrounding mountains of the Alaska range. Review Text:

Review Title: The highlight of our Alaskan Adventure
Review Text: The crew and office staff are amazing, friendly and helpful.  Bent over backwards to make our flight include a glacier landing since the weather was iffy.  Just can say enough about everyone we met.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: This is an exceptional activity, so worth every penny it cost. Our pilot was very smooth, and very knowledgeable. The office told us that the weather was unpredictable and that we might not be able to actually land on the glacier that day. We were told if we took the flight and could not land, we would not be charged for that part of the flight. It was a win-win so we took the flight. The sun came out just after we landed. After leaving the glacier and flying out of the mountains, we flew into a rainbow. Perfect day, very safe flight. So glad we chose to do this.

Review Title: Grand Denali w/ landing - magical. Make sure to use coupon.
Review Text:
Took Grand Denali tour with glacier landing - absolutely stunning. All 11 people in our party - parents with teenage kids - were totally blown away. The flyover of Mt. McKinley is phenomenal by itself; but the glacier landing provides a very impressive climax and I would strongly suggest to do it as well.
Having flown in small planes before, I was pleasantly surprised by the general smoothness of their ride in Alaska. I probably need to read up on why it is, but my gut feeling is that there is probably less turbulence in the air.
Would like to express gratitude to our pilot, Paul - very professional, personable, generally good to be around.
First important tip: at least this year Talkeetna Air Taxi had their coupon in Northern Lights coupon book; and it knocked about 20-25% off the grand total.
Secondly: I wish we realized ahead of time how cool of a destination the city of Talkeetna is, we might have spent a night there. Turns out it is a departure base for I believe all the climbers heading for Mt. McKinley, and the city has got quite a vibe.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text:
Having been in North and Southamerica, Africa, Europe, and Asia, there are a few experiences in my traveling life I will remember as highest points. This is one of them.

The flight to the highest peak of North America (more than 6.000 meters) and the landing on its glacier could sound risky or not for the faint of heart. Nothing more far from reality. And I can tell I fly a lot in commercial flights and experience in those big planes much more turbulences and discomforts than with this flight!!

All the flight (take-offs, movements among the peaks, landings) was executed smoothly, with perfect technique by the young pilot, whose name I cannot remember (only that he was from Arizona). Not only was he the pilot you feel perfectly safe with, but also he commented profusely all the trip about all kind of things we were seeing. Among them, a sublime avalanche in one of the surrounding peaks (far enough from us) minutes after we landed in the glacier. God-fearing awesome experience!!!

And worth every penny!!
(Not to talk of some of the most amazing photos I have ever taken)

Review Text: We had the most special experience... landscapes and views were awesome and the landing at the glacier was incredibly smooth!!!! The pilot was very professional and explained us every place we saw. We were lucky with weather codition, neverthelessI really recomend it!!! It's not cheap but if you can afford it, do it!

Review Title: Amazingly wonderful glacier landing plane ride
Review Text: Worth EVERY dollar!  This is a most incredible experience. The views are unforgettable. The feelings you get are phenomenal! These guys are the best!! If you do nothing else in Alaska and only this ride, you will have had the experience of a lifetime. Go early and pay the extra for landing on a glacier. Book this ahead of time, it fills up fast.

Review Text: My favorite activity on 10 day Alaska land trip! Worth the price tag. Drove from Anchorage (2.5 hours) AM for a 1:30 flight. Called ahead & requested earlier if possible to beat poor weather moving in, able to catch an 11:30 flight. 7 passengers. Incredible views of glacier valleys! Weather was partly cloudy so only saw about 2/3 of mountain. Very bumpy ride once we got near mountain. Pilot asked all aboard level of comfort & continued to Wick. Wall, then back to a nice wind protected glacier. This can be a very bumpy ride, but I'd do it again (not my wife!). Bring extra warm clothes, 30 minutes standing on glacier can be very cold! Felt like I could reach out and touch rock walls!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: My husband and I booked a glacier landing flight.  Talkeetna Air Taxi was very professional and helpful when we called to make the reservation.  It was one of the most amazing trips we have ever taken.  Our pilot Trent was friendly and knowledgable.  I was nervous but the take offsand landings we smooth.  I am glad I went.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: Our glacier landing family excursion was one the highlights of our Alaska vacation. And when I say family, I mean 2 adults and 3 kids (9, 8 and 1 year old). We all went and what an amazing experience it was! When planning our trip, we debated for weeks about having either each adult fly solo while the other one watch the kids or splitting 2 by 2 and taking the older ones. We decided on the 2 by 2 option and called Talkeetna Air to make the reservation. When we told the lady on the phone about our infant, she right away said "If you want, you can take the baby too". I have to say, I was a little nervous and had to think it over. Well, I am glad we took our little guy! We got to experience something really incredible as a family. Now taking kids on excursions like that requires some pre-planning. Our kids were all used to flying... but on commercial flights. I really wanted to make sure the older kids would be fine in a small plane. So a few weeks before the trip, I registered them for the EAA Young Eagles Program where volunteers take kids flying for free to make them discover the joy of flying (www.youngeagles.org). They both loved it and we knew we could take them on Denali! Now for the baby, the more I thought about it, I knew he would be fine as well. He is well traveled and a pretty laid back little fellow. Daniele was our pilot. She was great. She took the kids around the plane and showed them the inspection process and off we went! The baby was indeed fine... he actually fell asleep on the way there. Landing was breathtaking (literally!). The 2 older kids played in the snow, we took pictures and just enjoyed being at 5,000 feet in front of the Great One. It was a beautiful clear day. We were prepared with hats, gloves and heavy fleece. We did not need them. It was about 50-55 degrees on the glacier. Just perfect! Now It is true that it is far from cheap. We got a discount on the two older kids and the baby was free, but it was still a pretty penny. I guess for us, we don't buy the kids a lot of "stuff" even at Christmas. We just love going on pretty cool adventures!
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: My wife and I spent 3 days in Palmer, Ak B&B after 7 day cruise. Driving 100 miles to Talkeetna and flying around Mt McKinley was one of the best decisions we made. There were other folks offering flights. But, I can't imagine that they could be better than TAT. We booked our reservation by phone several months before we traveled. Very friendly staff and answered all my questions. We booked an 8:30 AM flight which came with a free glacier landing. They let me know that there was a certain amount of flexibility regarding time depending upon the weather. But, if "weathered out" of our 8:30 flight, the glacier landing would still be free. As it turns out, we had a beautiful sunny morning with no clouds. The pilot was very friendly, knowledgeable and an excellent "tour guide". My wife and I will probably not make it back to Alaska. But, I would highly recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi and see Mt McKinley by air.

Review Text:
Flight seeing in Alaska is a major investment, and this one is so worth the cost! Will, our pilot, was experienced and friendly... he made the trip even more worthwhile. You will never experience on a screen the reality of incredible views of Alaska, Denali, the majestic mountains, and endless vistas of Denali National Park. The glacier landing is a must if this is a one-time only visit. If you go on an early or late flight you get the glacier landing as a freebie. A must do, in my opinion.

Take non-drowsy Dramamine ahead of time if you tend toward motion sickness.

Review Text: Trevor, our pilot, was great, giving us information all along the way.  The company ADDED the glacier landing, saying WE were doing THEM a favor by letting them give it to us.  So kind and professional!  The day was PERFECT and that glacier landing allowed us to play in the snow!  Coming from 106 in Austin, TX, that was a blessing!   We will go back again.  Love love this company!  HIGHLY recommend them!

Review Text:
Wow. What can I say? The pictures that others have posted don’t lie. I woke at 7:00 a.m. on flight day and found thick, low-hanging clouds throughout the Talkeetna and area. I expected that the flight would be cancelled or I would be waiting for hours, but no. In fact, weather near the summit was crystal-clear with deep blue skies. I guess that’s just how variable weather can be in Alaska.

I went on the Grand Denali Tour by myself, and I was glad that they would accommodate me as a solo passenger. I picked the first flight of the day since that seems to be the best time of day for the weather. The flight was very smooth, even smoother than the flight to Anchorage on a 757. The pilot was very professional showing lots of sights and providing commentary. I could hear him and air traffic control through my headset, and I even enjoyed (LOL) hearing the Stall Warning as we descended for the glacier landing.

I spent about $315 total (somehow got the glacier landing for free) and I feel that it was well worth the price for me. But, I do only recommend this for adults and kids who truly appreciate the sights.

Review Title: I am walking on a glacier!
Review Text:
Usha, my wife, kept saying "I am walking on a glacier!" after we stepped out of our craft on Ruth Glacier on Mt. McKinley. It was a bright and sunny day, we saw the Denali peak very clearly. Our pilot, Doug, had more than thirty years of experience flying small craft near the peaks of the Alaskan range.

We got many views of the peaks and it was a fully satisfying experience! I guess we were lucky because the weather was great!

Review Text:
We booked the 8:30 flight with TAT well in advance, with an early bird discount. On the day of the flight, the weather was questionable. "Not a problem - you can go, or reschedule if your schedule permits, or we'll fully refund you". We decided to wait a few hours and see. A couple of hours later, I called them again. TAT, very cheerfully, "the weather is still not clear. Let us know". We decided not to take a chance, and cancelled. an hour later we meet a couple that returned from the 8:30 flight (which we did not take). According to them, the weather over the mountain is OK. We went to TAT again and asked when can we do the flight. TAT: "Now!".
40 minutes later we were over the mountain. What an experience. Truly out of this world. Something you have to experience.

Our pilot (Tyler) was just as professional and nice as the receptionists. he made sure we all felt comfortable and safe, shared his experience and knowledge without yapping at us the whole flight. On the way back, he took advantage of the weather (light rain and sun) to show us a full-circle rainbow. What a cool dude.

Bottom line: they are professional, welcoming, and interested in you, not only your wallet. The flight and glacier landing are amazing. Take the landing option.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: I had planned our Talkeetna Air Taxi excursion in advance and the weather was looking cloudy and showery on the day of the reservation.  TAT was wonderful in allowing me to rebook a couple of days earlier to catch a patch of great weather.  I am older person not quite yet at AARP age, but getting close.  I was a little concerned climbing in and out of these things.  I had no problems (it may not have been the most graceful :).  For anyone concerned about the "weigh in"...it is discreet....you get on a scale, but no one but the person behind the desk sees the number.  Check in was quick and efficient.  I used a Northern Lights coupon which saved us 25% off a party of four.  Do this if you can....definitely a highlight of the trip.

Review Text: Thank you to all those at Talkeetna Air Taxi! I had a remarkable time. I felt very safe. I was co pilot in the landing on Mt. McKinley when we went. Great energy from the pilot. Friendly staff. Everything went very well. This is one of my favorite memories of all time, so thank you!!

Review Text:
On Wednesday, August 7th, we arrived at TAT at 4:00 pm for a 4:30 reservation for our party of four. As soon as we got to the desk we were shown a relief map of the area surrounding Mt. McKinley (Denali) and we were told that the cloud cover would prevent us from seeing the peaks. However, they had been making glacier landings all day. I discussed it with my party and told the staff that we'd go ahead as long as they were making landings. They again said they've been making landings all day.
We put on the supplied over boots and boarded the plane. Just before we taxied away someone spoke to our pilot and I'm pretty sure he said something to the effect that the air had become choppy and a landing would not be possible but that he should fly around a little more.
The flight was amazing but when we approached the glacier where he would have landed he told us the air was too choppy for a landing. When we returned to the hangar the pilot said that if we had paid for a glacier landing there would be an adjustment made.
I went back to the counter where another party was just instructed to put on their over boots.
I informed the staff at the counter that we didn't land on the glacier and that I was annoyed that they let us fly knowing that we had discussed it at the beginning and that we were going ahead with the flight with limited visibility because they had been making landings all day.
One of the women said that they never guarantee a glacier landing because the weather is so changeable. I said but the pilot was told before we taxied away that there wouldn't be a landing and that we could have just as easily waited for the next day. She said, "We'll, you can try again tomorrow if you like." I'm not sure, but I don't think she was offering us a free flight, so, yeah for another $1100.00 we could try agin tomorrow. Thanks.
They refunded us $85.00 per person plus the $10.00 per person Denali park fee.
Here's the thing. The flight was incredible. Not the issue. The people are really nice. Not the issue. The pilot was incredibly knowledgeable and gave us fantastic views. Not the issue.
The issue is we were only going ahead because of the landing and before we left they knew we wouldn't be able to. Not only that, as far as I know, they didn't inform he people after us either.
We rented a car and drove from Anchorage, booked a bed and breakfast, spent a day in Talkeetna after a cruise from Vancouver and the highlight of our time in Alaska was going to be landing on a glacier. Yes, there was no guarantee that if we waited until Thursday we would have made a landing. No guarantee. But, it was a sure bet that before we took off they knew we weren't making a landing. Guaranteed.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: When we visited Denali National Park, the clouds obscured Mt. McKinley, as it does frequently. We made a last minute decision to take a flight over the mountains and glaciers. Several people we met in the park highly recommended Talkeetna Air Taxi so we booked a flight which included landing on a glacier. Our excellent pilot  maneuvered around mountain peaks and glaciers giving us a spectacular view of Mt. McKinley.  Landing on the glacier was icing on the cake. We enjoyed it so much we were tempted to book another flight!  Even if you see Mt. McKinley, it is very worthwhile to do this flight.  Definitely the highlight of our trip.
