Review Text: Booked our glacier landing on a whim as we walked through town. If you do the first flight (8:00am) or the last one out (6:00pm) they give you the landing for the price of the fly over. Dud the last flight at 6pm and  I think we paid $199 each to land in the glacier and capture the most gorgeous photos on film and in our memories! Pilot was outstanding.  Very knowledgeable, patient and professional.  They also give you a last minute chance to change your mind before you go up if the clouds are obstructing the summit and fully refund your money. No tricks or gimmicks, they want you to enjoy your flight and get your money's worth.

Review Text: We took the South Face McKinley Tour with glacier landing and it was an unforgettable experience. The views of the mountains, including Mount McKinley (peeping out above the clouds), and several glaciers are amazing. The glacier landing was fun, especially being able to take photos with the plane on the snow. The company is very professional: the booking process was smooth, they answered all of our questions in no time, and also in explaining the safety issues they gave us the impression they clearly knew what they were doing.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We took the 2 hour Grand Denali Tour with a glacier landing on August 2nd.  There is no question this was the highlight of our time in Alaska.  The majesty of the mountains and the beauty of the daunting wilderness are made intimate, real, and inspiring on this flight.  Nothing can prepare you for the power of the mountains up close, or for their enormity as experienced when you land, not just on A glacier, but a glacier surrounded by the peaks of the tallest mountains on the continent.  This was very,  very special and worth every penny.   In addition, we were very impressed with the care, security, focus, and knowledge of our pilot, and with our aircraft.  We flew in a 10 passenger Otter that had plenty of room for everyone, was equipped with bubble windows which made photography from the plane possible, and provided a smooth turbulence free ride.  Our pilot (whose name I am sorry to say I did not get) was extremely knowledgeable of not only the mountains, but the history of efforts to climb Denali and the geologic process that forms and transforms glaciers.  He even spotted a Moose swimming in a lake below us on the flight!   On the ground, the staff provided first class service.  We arrived in Talkeetna early on the day before we were scheduled to fly and checked in to make sure we knew the lay of the land.  It was a perfect day and Denali was crystal clear in the distance.  The staff asked us if we would like to fly in that afternoon since they had room on a late afternoon flight, and the weather report for the next day was for overcast skies and a shower or two.  We readily agreed, and while the weather the next day was fine for a flight, it wasn’t as good as that afternoon and so they helped make a great experience a spectacular one.  Talkeetna Air Taxi personnel were just top notch, A-one, the best.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Nice flight tour...not a perfect day
Review Text:
We could not do a Glacier Landing...and from talking with folks, I don't think these happen very often (although they are advertised as a big part of the experience). The flight was good...pilot was young, but did a great job. We did get nice shots of Denali...but it was still fairly cloudy.

They do (as advertised) talk about the conditions and let you make the choice on whether or not you want to fly (or refund)...I am glad we flew.

Review Text: We had a great glacier landing. Ths s a must do in Alaska. They even picked us up from our hotel. They have free glacier landing with flight seeing tours in the late afternoon.

Review Text: I've gone zip-lining in the Costa Rican rainforest, snorkeled with sea turtles in the Barbados and crewed on an America's Cup yacht in St Martin, but my recent sightseeing flight into Denali National Park with Talkeetna Air Taxi just may have been the coolest thing I've ever done!  From the time my wife and I started planning our recent two week trip to Alaska, at the top of my to-do list was a sightseeing flight into Denali National Park!  I reserved a morning flight with a free glacier landing on the Saturday of the July 4th weekend, but woke up that morning to overcast, drizzly skies.  Arriving at the TAT office, I was informed my flight had been canceled due to the weather.  I was given the option of getting my deposit refunded or rescheduling for later that day or the next.  As we were leaving Talkeetna for the Kenai peninsula the next morning, later that day was the only choice if I was to fly.  I opted for a 6:30 pm flight, hoping the weather would clear by then.  I arrived back at TAT that evening to find that planes were flying, although foggy and warm conditions up in Denali would most likely prevent a glacier landing and keep Mt McKinley mostly shrouded.  I was once again given the choice of a refund due to the conditions, but I wanted to fly!  As there was only one other couple going up with me, we were to fly in a Dehaviland Beaver, a great classic aircraft!  Our friendly pilot explained the safety regulations and pointed out the location of all safety gear in case of emergency prior to boarding.  Then we were up, up and away!  En route our pilot told us if at all possible, we'd land on the glacier, but it was unlikely due to fog at the various landing sites and sticky snow, due to the warmer weather.  He told us how just a week earlier a flight had been forced to land on the glacier due to a sudden storm and were stranded there for 4 days, unable to take off due to the snow conditions.  Point taken- not worth risking the landing unless conditions were prime!  If the scenery approaching Denali was amazing, the views once we entered the mountain range were just flat out  breathtaking!  Our pilot pointed out the various mountains and glaciers as he guided us expertly thru the passes, walls of rock and snow seemingly close enough to touch at times!  As expected, the upper half of Mt McKinley was shrouded in fog, but he took us around the lower flanks pointing out various points of interest.  Since we couldn't land on the glacier, he gave us an extra long time touring the peaks, before turning back to Talkeetna.  Upon arriving back at the TAT office, I was informed they were discounting my flight 10% due to the conditions preventing the glacier landing. Was I disappointed we didn't land on the glacier or get to see Mt McKinley in all it's glory?  Of course, but that doesn't mean it wasn't an absolutely awesome, jaw-dropping experience!  If your trip to Alaska brings you anywhere near the Talkeetna area, be sure to put a sightseeing flight with Talkeetna Air Taxi at the top of your list!

Review Title: A vacation highlight without a doubt.
Review Text:
I had checked the web site for Talkeetna Air Taxi well over two years ago and I knew we had to do this trip, even before reading all the information. The flight booking for the four of us was no problem and we knew we would be safe in one of their famous “DeHavilland Otters”. When the big day finally arrived, and all the preliminaries dealt with, we were introduced to our pilot, a terrific young man, who also proved to be an excellent photographer as well. His expertise in the "Otter" was reassuring, as was his commentary about the area. Upon approaching Mt. McKinley through the cloud it looked like our views of the mighty mountain were going to be brief, but after crossing to the other side, it was as if a curtain had been lifted and as we looked to our right, there it was in all of it’s glory. We were in clear blue sky and what a magical sight the mountain presented. This was a photographers dream and I managed to capture some amazing images, both still and moving. The pilot decided to land on Buckskin Glacier, just to the side of Moose’s Tooth, a jagged peak seemingly not to far from McKinley, yet 23 kilometers away. The landing was like landing on a cushion, the snow soft and pure. The eight passengers onboard then spent a wondrous time experiencing the isolation and the sheer majesty of this pristine location. This was a life changing experience for most of us, and that included all four of our party. The take off and departure from the head of the valley and the subsequent flight over the very tip of Moose’s Tooth was another highlight. We then glided over and then down the other side, following other glaciers that appeared to be everywhere. Small planes flew underneath us, thousands of feet below, all going in different directions to unknown destinations. The remainder of the trip was just a blur of snow, big mountains and the ever present, yet spectacular glaciers.
I would love to do it all again and I strongly urge anyone with thoughts of doing this flight to go for it. The weather will be your only obstacle.

Review Text:
OK this was the plane ride and glacier landing experience. This is one of those thing you do and it is a once in a life time experiences. AMAZING. So how is Talkeetna Air Taxi involved? Well they fly you around the Mountains, most notably Denali AKA Mt. McKinley and land you on a glacier. I would guess that if the weather is not good it could be disappointing. Here is how Talkeetna Air Taxi helped us out. On our way to Talkeetna, my husband was concerned that the weather would not be good for our plane ride/viewing and glacier landing so he called and asked if they could get us in that evening. They called us back and scheduled us for an evening flight that day. Once we arrived in Talkeetna and the day went on, thunderstorms (yep it was so hot there they actually got a thunderstorm, which is very rare). Knowing it would blow over we went to our scheduled appointment time. It had gotten windy. My husband spoke with the employees and a pilot, who said we could still go up, but he thought the next day would be better. So they rescheduled us again. The next day, the day we were originally supposed to go was perfect. So I am grateful they allowed us to change and then change again our flight seeing and glacier landing.

We used the NorthernLights Coupon Book (Like the entertainment book) to save some money. I believe the coupon was save on a group booking (four or more), so we saved several hundred dollars.

Our pilot and the other passengers (11 total on board the place) had great views of the terrain below and the mountains. The pilot was extremely knowledgeable about the history of the land, geology ect. He made many passes around Denali so each side of the plane could get good views and pictures (place was one seaters each side). Smooth landing on the glacier and we stayed about 30 minutes. We asked the pilot lots of questions about the glacier, the indigenous peoples of Alaska etc and he answered them all. he also took lots of peoples pictures. The ride home was just as cool as we went along the Ruth glacier and he educated us on the glacier and about glaciers.

If you have the opportunity, this is a MUST DO!!!!!! I couldn't help but feel after this experience that we were blessed to have people who use their gift of flying to bring something like Denali and glaciers so close to us and to share it with us up close and personal.

Review Title: even on a cloudy day: it's well worth it!
Review Text:
When we made our booking for july 7th 2012, I was sure that we would have the same perfect weatherconditions like a lot of other guests had (don't ask me why I was so sure about it). Well, that was wrong. We were scheduled on an early morning flight with glacier landing. We woke up at 5 o'clock in the morning by the sound of the pouring rain = not the very best start. Our flight was cancelled and we asked if we could reschedule on a later flight the same day (we had to continue to Denali NP the same evening). => next try: late afternoon (what gave us the possibilty to go on a Jet Boat Tour (Mahay's Jet Adventure) which turned out to be interesting) When we came back to Talkeetna Air Taxi they finally decided to start the flight. I'm sure it would have been beautiful with sunshine. But: we had the clouds, and it was different, but very interesting: it's amazing how many different colours of gray and blue and white the glaciertongues have. Our pilot (Tylor) was "climbing" up through the clouds, looking for "wholes" in the clouds (getting close to the mountains) and doing a perfect landing on the glacier. Even if we know glaciers (we're from Switzerland): a glacier landing is very special, also to us.

Special: Due to the weatherconditions, Tylor could not do the whole flight we had booked, and I was surprised that we got the difference paid back

What we also appreciated: Talkeetna Air Taxi prefers to cancel or shorten a flight instead of taking too many risks - the friendlyness of the people
If we ever make our way back to Alaska: we'll try it again: hopefully with sunshine
Thank you!

Review Title: A Most Amazing Experience - Flight and Glacier Landing
Review Text:
I booked a flightseeing trip with the Talkeetna Air Taxi through the Alaska Railroad reservation services in mid-April. It was the most wonderful experience! I had checked the 7-day weather forecast and saw that the weather on that Saturday would be perfect, no cloud cover. The TAT provides complimentary hotel pick-up, and a very nice young gentleman picked me up, along with others I had met on the train who were staying at another hotel.

We arrived at the TAT office at the flightline, and we all lined up to be weighed and outfitted with shoe covers for those without snowboots. I looked around and noted that Adam Richman (of Man vs. Food fame) had been a celebrity customer. He had left an autographed photo for the TAT staff to hang on their wall.

The flight started out with a safety briefing and we all boarded with great anticipation. The airplane was a De Havilland Canada DHC-3 Otter. We were provided headphones to listen to the flightseeing narrative by the pilot. It wasn't until I returned home to discover the call-sign "Zero Papa Romeo" referred to the last three letters/numbers on the aircraft (0PR).

We flew around the peaks of Denali, and then for the highlight, landed very smoothly on the Sheldon Amphitheater on Ruth Glacier. It was so nice chatting with the other passengers all in excitement of what we were experiencing. We hopped out and started snapping photos of each other, of the terrain, of the Sheldon Mountain House (and yes, the outhouse with a lady exiting). When someone asked the pilot which peak was Denali, he pointed up to a peak way up high and so tiny above us and to the left. It was difficult to fathom exactly how high Denali actually was. The takeoff was amazing! It was as if we were in a helicopter! It took very little distance to lift off of the glacier snow. It was explained the turboprop made all the difference compared to the days of the old Cessna planes.

I cannot do any more than to recommend that this should be added to everyone's "bucket list." It was so wonderful!

Review Text: My son (late 20's) and I took the flightseeing tour on April 4, 2013.  We were in Anchorage and called to make a reservation. The staff was very friendly and worked to schedule a time that was both convenient for us ~ allowing us plenty of time to get there - 2.5 hrs from Anchorage ~ and not be rushed. It also allowed us to get a bite to eat in Talkeetna, since our flight was going to be shortly after lunch. Though the weather may seem warm outside, take a jacket and gloves, the glacier air is cold.  Sunglasses are a must because of the glare from the snow. If you forget them, you can get a set upon registering at the check in desk. 'Over boots' are provided for your shoes, and they cover your leg to approx mid calf. Though I had ankle top hiking boots on, the rubber boots fit easily over them. My son was in tennis shoes and he was fine with the overboots. His feet did not get wet.  The plane is small, so you will have a tight fit, but it is well worth it, once you see what is in store for you. The beauty and majesty of the mountains fills you with awe. Our pilot was very knowledgeable and pointed out interesting features of not only the mountains, terrain, and surrounding area, but the glacier itself. Landing on the glacier was a thrill. The beauty and quiet has such a sense of peace. You feel as if you're in another world. There is plenty of opportunity for picture taking and strolling around.  I took a lot of pics on the flight to the glacier and was beginning to think my camera battery would die, but it didn't. I would encourage you to take your pics on the flight TO the glacier because that is where the bulk of your trip is going to take place. You fly through many areas of the mountains before you reach the glacier. The trip back to Talkeetna airport was picturesque for the first 15 min or so, but I didn't take as many pics as on the way up. There were only 2 drawbacks for me: I have difficulty getting into the small planes ~ so it's not graceful ~ there's no easy way to get in them. Secondly, I was sitting up front, so maybe the noise was louder from the propeller, but I had to strain at times to hear the pilot's narrative on our flight. It could be also that he may not have been speaking loud enough. My son is a private pilot and after our trip, he commented to me on how well the pilot flew the plane. In previous flights on small planes we've experienced slight nausea, but neither of us did this time.  I felt very relaxed, safe and secure on this flight and would highly recommend this flightseeing tour. If you're in Ak for a short time, this is a must if the weather is in your favor on your trip.  Enjoy it!   ( Waiting for our flight we learned that this air taxi is also a shuttle for mountaineers preparing to hike the mountains or ascend Denali. So this company has a lot of experience flying into the mountains and landing on the glaciers.)  This is a very professional team and safety is a priority.  I would definitely use this company again.  The Lees - Culpeper, VA

Review Title: Once in a lifetime experience - landing on Mt. Denali
Review Text:
We took a flight with Talkeetna Air Taxi to fly around Denali National Park and Mt. McKinley and then land on the Ruth glacier on Mt. McKinley (about 6,000 ft). It was a calm and crystal clear day so it was a breathtaking experience.

Talkeetna Air and our pilot were very professional and friendly.

It was one of the best experiences of our life.

Review Text: We booked this flightseeing tour in advance of our Alaska trip based on tripadvisor reviews and we were not disappointed! When we first arrived in Talkeetna it was overcast and rainy so our flight was postponed. The staff at TAT were very friendly and helpful with rescheduling our flight. We arrived early and checked back throughout the day but with no break in the weather we were forced to reschedule. I would stress that you should try to plan an alternate date in your trip in case you have to cancel due to weather. Luckily our flightseeing trip was scheduled before our trip to Denali National Park and we were able to reschedule for the day we left Denali which turned out to be gorgeous! We arrived early as instructed, were checked in quickly and found out we were being upgraded from the basic south face tour w/ glacier landing to the full grand summit tour! We boarded a small plane with only two other people and set out almost immediately. The scenery is spectacular. If you're coming to Alaska with a goal of seeing Denali this is the only way to truly "see" it. Our tiny Cessna flew up and down glacial gorges, made a 360 degree circuit of the summit, and made a perfect ski landing on the snow-covered Ruth Glacier. This was one of the best experiences we had in Alaska and money well-spent. If you splurge on one big excursion in your Alaska vacation, make it this one.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: viewing Denali by air and landing on a glacier the most amazing experience
Review Text: My husband and I were one of the last flights of the day and we flew in the tiniest Cessna and I felt like I was knee-to-knee with our pilot. The Cessnas are specially modified to land on glaciers and fly at these altitudes and in Alaskan weather so it was all very safe and our pilot experienced and professional. Talkeetna Air Taxi have other larger planes but we were the last ones for the day and we were pleased to experience a 'private' Grand Denali tour with glacier landing. If there is inclimate weather, see if you can wait another day or try to be flexible in your travel itinerary because it's worth it to do the glacier landing and get views of Denali. The weather was iffy on our day so we chose to wait around and then were in luck to be able to land on one of the smaller glaciers. You see so many glaciers that it really didn't matter to us which glacier we landed on as there are so many to view. I'm glad we chose to go with Talkeetna Air Taxi as it was nice to do the flightseeing from Talkeetna itself. And we did get intermittent views of Denali despite the not-so-perfect day. Well worth the money.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Title: Was the highlight if our vacation.
Review Text: Whe booking anything in AK, always try to have a back up date/ plan, when it comes to weather related plans. While heading to Denali our plan was to take a glacier flight/ landing around Mt. Mc Kinley. We arrived as planned but learned due yo the wildfires a flight was impossible. They were very apologetic and helped us come up with a plan. Luckily we would be passing Talkeenta on our way to Seward and we would try again. Luckily it was a picture perfect/ smoke free day so there definitely be a flight. Unfortunately because so many flights were rebooked like ours, our flight was booked solid. Our pilot came out looked us straight in the eye( holding all our info) and said because this is a booked solid flight, it is important that none of us fudged our weight#'s and if he thought we did he would have no problem bringing out a scale. Although if this was at any other place I may have been upset or insulted. Instead I appreciated the safety measures that they think is necessary. Our flight was amazing and the mountain was out the whole time. Lots of photo ops. The glacier landing was by far one of the coolest things I have ever had a chance to do.  I highly recommend that if u are willing to do the flight, go ahead and pay extra for the landing. You may never have an opportunity like this again. Once we landed we took pictures for what seemed like 15 minutes and gawked at the mountains surrounding us. On our flight back we saw a few moose and a beaver damn. During the flight the pilot provided us with info on geology and wildlife in the area. The best part was I found a coupon for this in a magazine that I got at the airport. So be on the look out.... I believe it was a 10% off!!! If I ever drive up towards Talkeenta again this will definitely be on my yo do list .... Coupon or not!!!

Review Text: This is a first class operation.  Sea Otter airplanes are well taken care of.  Starts out with outfitting of "glacier boots" and before loading, a safety talk and a briefing on the flight.  Everybody gets on.  I ended up in the copilot seat (no controls) going up.  Coming back someone else asked to be there, so no problem.  Everybody has a window, and the pilot turns the plane constantly so everybody gets a good view.  Our pilot would point out many interesting features of the mountain, as well as some history and a little "Glacier 1A."  The landing on the glacier is of course the highlight.  Don't miss this!  Oh, yeah, everyone gets headphones so you can hear the chatter on the radio.  In addition to landing and take-off communications, the pilots up there talk to each other about visibility and mountain conditions.  Really interesting.  Our ten year old granddaughter was too afraid to look out of the plane, but really loved it out on the glacier where she was dancing around and laughing.

Review Text:
Good communication via phone. $270 bought us a plane ride + glacier landing. The airport was super busy on a beautiful day. They have a deck out back where you can watch all the planes. They gave us sunglasses and boots for the glacier. Pilot (tom?) was excellent, and gave a great tour as he flew. Plane ride was smooth. The return had a few bumps, I did have mild nausea in the back, which I'm prone to. Sitting in front was better and very cool.

DO NOT EAT THE GLACIER SNOW. They always land there (3 planes were on the glacier while we were there). I'm sure some kids/people must have urinated there before. It's always cold, so waste is not going anywhere. Just Sayin'

Overall, decide first if you think it's worth so much money for such a short experience. Before going, I was very ambivalent about the value. In retrospect, there is no other way to see the mountains/Denali so closely.

The safety issue is also important to me. I do *think* they are very conservative, because they won't sell the longer tours with marginal weather. The pilot had many years experience.

Talkeetna is a cool place.

Review Text:
We had signed up for the “Grand Denali” tour with a glacier landing. The glacier landing was free due to an early reservation that we made online. Check in was simple – step on a scale so they can verify your weight and then head out back to grab some light boots to cover our shoes for the glacier landing. The pilot gives a quick rundown of the plane and what to expect on the trip. We were scheduled to fly on their newly renovated DeHavilland Otter and there were nine people, including the pilot, on our flight.

We take off and fly north towards Denali and can see forever because of the clear skies - the pilot shared plenty of information about the area via our headphones. We follow the Tokositna and Ruth Glaciers and end up circling Denali until the pilot brings the plane down for the glacier landing. Step off the plane surrounded by mountains in such a remote spot – totally worth it. I would say the flight to/from the glacier landing was about 45 minutes each way and we spent about 30 minutes on the glacier (2-hours total). I would highly recommend this tour with TAT and recommend the glacier landing, even if you have to pay the additional cost.

Review Text: One of the best ways to see Alaska is from the air! Our pilot flew us across the beautiful plains straight toward Mt. Whitney and after flying us over and through the mountains we landed on a glacier. You pay a little more for this experience, but it is worth every single penny. Review Title: A professional outfit with a modern fleet of aircraft and informative pilot/guides.
Review Text: We were blessed with amazing weather during our stay in Talkeetna so decided to book a flightsee last minute.  Our host at our lodging gave us a few to choose from and we settled on TAT.  We called them up and they told us that if we got to the airport within 15 minutes we could get on the next flight on the best flying day they'd had in weeks. Review Text:
When I saw TAT's website I was hooked. Would I be able to convince the other 5 people in my party, two of whom live in Anchorage? I gave my best shot, "We traveled many hours to get to Alaska, this was an expensive adventure, but we were actually flying round North America's magestic Mt. McKinley, but you only live once." Review Text:
Great experience - it won't be forgotten. Excellent organization and service; they did their very best. Expensive.

I booked several months in advance so I could get an early-morning flight in late June, 2012. There was a certain deposit with that - perhaps $150. When we showed up the morning of the flight, the HQ crew did a good job keep expectations where they belonged, because clouds / fog can come in over Denali at any time. Due to TAT's size, they had an early plane already on the way up to the mountain - probably with hiker supplies - and they were able to get a firsthand weather report from that plane. My daughter had dressed for weather in Talkeetna and one of the front desk ladies loaned her a coverup / light jacket because the glacier landing isn't exactly warm. After the weather report, we met our pilot (who was young, handsome, and turned my wife into a babbling mess because of it - but no worries), then boarded the plane, and took off. There were just three of us as passengers, plus the pilot - it was really a private flight. We quickly arrived at the mountains and it's remarkable how close you can fly to them on a calm day - being right next to the snowy cliffs in the clear air was amazing. If you have questions about something the pilot was able to tip the plane to get a better look, or circle around to a better example . . . you can also hear other planes over the headphone, and spot them flying around. We did the glacier landing and it was smooth - not scary at all. Getting out at base camp and having the high walls of the mountain above you is just fantastic, and my daughter and I enjoyed running around on the snow. Flying back was a breeze; the whole thing was great and a touch otherworldly. Highly recommended if you can afford it - it's not cheap. Save up.

Review Text: Despite a weather cancellation on day 1 and a plane stuck on the glacier on day 2 the folks at TAT went out of their way to get us up in the air for our flight see and glacier landing. Review Text: We took the Grand Denali flight with glacier landing.  The entire staff in the office was friendly and helpful.  I was nervous, having never flown in such a small plane.  A nice lady behind the desk reassured me and eased my fears.  We flew in a 5 seater plane, and Tim was our pilot.  Like the people in the office, Tim was professional, informative, and friendly.  He helped us into our seats, made sure we were buckled properly, and had our headsets working.  I couldn't believe the flight was so smooth!  Tim was an excellent pilot and tour guide - he answered all of our questions, and maneuvered the plane so that everyone could see everything out of their own window.  The views were stunning!  We had a sunny day, with a few clouds near Denali, but could clearly see the mountain and surrounding areas.  I took well over 100 pictures.  We landed on Ruth Glacier.  If you are able to add a glacier landing to your flight, do it!  Walking on a glacier and seeing the mountains towering over us was just incredible!  Bring sunglasses though, since there is glare from the snow.  Flying with TAT was the highlight of my Alaska vacation, and if I ever make it back, I will definitely fly with them again.

Review Text:
My girlfriend and I pulled into Talkeetna around 2:30 pm, on a Tuesday in early July. We had a reservation to take a flight tour around Mt. McKinley/Denali for 5:30. Talkeetna Air Taxi(TAT) told us to come in when we got to town to check in with them. When we got there, they told us the mountain had been clear all day so far, despite contrary weather reports(which are useless here anyways). We asked about going out the next day, due to more promising forecasts. But, they suggested going out right then. So, within 15 minutes we were on our way up in a plane. The plan was that we were to do the Base Camp Tour(yellow line). From the time we got up in the air, it was pretty clear that Mt. McKinley was in complete cloud cover. Once we were up in the mountains, we could see VERY little. Some decent views of glaciers, which were pretty spectacular, but no mountain peaks. At all. We did land on the glacier at base camp for about 5 minutes. Same visibility story on the way down, except that we didn't finish our route, we just came back the way we had already come. All in all a disappointing experience. I don't blame TAT for that. The weather is quite unpredictable, there is no denying that.

HOWEVER.. The next morning, I called them as soon as they opened and talked to Annie, the office manager. After expressing my disappointment from the previous days experience, she offered to let us take another flight that morning for a significant discount if we could be there in ten minutes. With clear blue skies(a rarity) above, I said yes and abruptly shook my girlfriend awake so we could get from the Talkeetna Hostel, just a few blocks away to the office. We got there and checked in and again, within just a few minutes we were working our way into a much smaller craft. What we had awaiting us was a COMPLETELY different experience. We immediately had clear views of Denali in the distance and a beautiful day in general. The tour that Annie put us on, must have been the best tour they offered, because we were given an informed and intimate introduction to not only the summit of Denali, but many other peaks around. The other passengers were a father and son, the elder of which, summited Denali and several other major peaks throughout the Alaska Range. As such, our pilot Tyler took us pretty much everywhere that you could get to. He was a knowledgeable, excellent and thoughtful pilot and tour guide. We could not have imagined such a fantastic experience, but it was a highlight of our two week visit.

Thanks to Annie, Tyler and everyone else at TAT. Great company that clearly cares about their customers, their business and their reputation. I appreciate that sort of integrity and commitment, and would have no problems telling anyone to choose them for their flight tours.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: We were a party of 4 (2 adults, 2 kids, 8 & 9) and we booked the South face Tour with Glacier Landing. However, the 1st day when we were supposed to go up was a rainy day and TAT rescheduled our flight on a later date, the day we would be driving back from Denali to Anchorage. The weather was not the best even on the second time, however, it was not raining and we decided to go ahead with the flight. At first, my wife was a little apprehensive of flying in a small plane (an 8-seater DeHavilland Beaver). There was 10-20 miles/hr wind and I was a little concerned too. However, the flight was very smooth. As the plane started to climb higher, the landscape beneath started to change from forest to rivers with sandbars to glacier. Soon the excitement took over any fear we had at the beginning. Finally the landing on Kahiltna glacier was the climax of the entire flight. We went crazy taking pictures. We were on the glacier for almost half hour but it seemed very short. Even though everyone has a window seat, the best viewpoint, I think, is from the 2nd row passenger seating where my wife was seated. This flightseeing tour was certainly at the top of all other highlights of our great Alaskan trip. I would do it again in a heartbeat.
Disclaimer: This review is the subjective opinion of a Tripadvisor member and not of Tripadvisor LLC.

Review Text: I booked this excursion on line after learning about TAT in a travel section article in the Washington Post.  The admin staff got us registered on line and when we arrived at the airstrip we were prepped for the flight in a short amount of time.  The aircraft was a 10- 12 passenger DeHavilland Turboprop that had plenty of juice to handle the type of flying for this trip.  Our pilot and guide seemed rather young, but after just several minutes in the air it was obvious he was extremely capable of handling the aircraft and he provided excellent narration about the terrain we were flying over.  Although there were a lot of clouds in the area our pilot threaded his way through them and within 30 minutes had us circling the two summits of Mt McKinley.  Then he circled around several glaciers and landed in the Ruth Glacier in a magical area known as the "Amphitheater".  It was almost a religious experience to walk on a snow -packed glacier surrounded by 10K peaks all around us.  We spent 20-25 minutes in this "Cathedral in the Alaska Range" before heading back to Talkeetna.  Oh yes, I got to sit in the co-pilot seat on the return flight to get a real bird's eye view of the amazing Alaskan lanscape.  I can not say enough good things about our experience with Talkeetna Air Taxi.  Yes, it seems expensive at first glance but I can tell you it was worth every penny.  I would do it again in a heartbeat.

We were loaded into the Otter and our pilot Bill? sounded so encouraging and confident I couldn't help but start to calm down.  The day began overcast but warm.  Our pilot flew us in to the only open patch of blue sky and low and behold we got our first glimpse of the mountain known as Denali.  We landed on the ice and were surprised by the warm temperature. Review Text:
You want to see Mt. McKinley? Do it properly, OK it's a but expensive but the experience is once in a lifetime. You really do fly close to the mountains with knowledgeable commentary from a highly skilled, extremely competent pilot.

As a wheelchair user they were very helpful and let me direct the assistance, There is a real "can do " attitude with the office and ground crew staff.

I am an active wheelchair user and a high level transfer is required to get into the back of the aircraft so was able to sit in the front seat. However, weaker wheelchair users may struggle to get in the aircraft.

Review Title: Everyone is not exaggerating... You've GOT to do this!
Review Text: If you go to Alaska and don't do the flightseeing tour, you are truly missing out on one of the highlights of your trip.  It was one of the highlights of my life!  I was leery of going in a small plane flying through the mountains and landing on a glacier, and told my husband I'd stay back while he went alone.  I didn't want him to miss out on something he really wanted to do, so I went reluctantly.  The staff were very friendly and knowledgeable, and if the weather is bad, they will postpone your trip until it's clear enough to go.  You can trust them if they tell you the weather is clear above the clouds, they know their stuff and have a great safety record.  They are the ones who take the mountain climbers up to climb Mt. McKinley to the base camp.  First, they give you glacier boots so your feet aren't cold, and will have good traction walking on the glacier when you land.  The views are mind blowing, and there are really no words to describe them, other than you will feel like you are watching an IMAX movie.  Your pictures from the plane will be amazing, and the ride is as smooth as can be.  It's great to see the Talkeetna area from the plane, flying over the vast green Alaskan wilderness.  Once you get to the mountains,  it's will take your breath away, and seeing such beauty brought tears to my eyes.  Our pilot was friendly and professional, and did a super job flying the plane.  He told us he had been flying with them for over five years.  All I can say is it's worth every penny, and I'd do it again in a heartbeat. I wish I could  share all of my pictures because every one is a masterpiece!  Don't hesitate, it's the best!!!

Review Title: Must do in Alaska! Friendly staffs!
Review Text:
This is a great tour and must do when you go to Alaska. The staffs are great and very helpful.
I showed up very early for my flight and requested if any earlier flight available. A sweet staff not only booked me on a earlier flight but also upgraded to a better one with no charge as there was space available. She could have asked me to wait or asked to pay the difference but she gladly upgraded with a friendly smile.
Like most of Alaska, this tour is totally weather dependent. Rainy & cloudy weather are very common in Alaska so be prepared. I visited during the first week of July. Its been pretty much cloudy all day when I was there and not lucky enough to see Mt.Denali from the ground. But I was fortunate enough to view all the peaks including Denali above the clouds from the flight. Our pilot is very friendly, knowledgeable and did a great job flying through the peaks. The views are incredible, breathtaking and possibly the best thing happened in my whole week-long Alaska trip. The cost is pretty much comparable to any flight tours in lower 48 so do not miss this because it's expensive, you may regret not doing this later because this could be an once in a lifetime experience.

Review Title: Bubble windows on TAT are great for viewing/photography.
Review Text: My wife and I did Grand Denali tour with TAT and it was wonderful.  This was our 2nd tour with TAT.  We did the same tour last year, but the weather was not as good.  Our flight was cancelled due to weather, and we hung around Talkeetna during the day and did eventually get to go out.  It was great, but not as great as this recent trip (because of the better weather).  For this visit, I did not book anything in advance.  I figured I would just wait, and if the weather was good, I would try to book something last minute, and if not, we would just enjoy food and drink in Talkeetna. Our first morning in Talkeenta was very clear with Mckinley in full view, so I called TAT was able to get 2 seats on an 8:30 am departure (if you have a larger party, it might be tough to do this, but for only 2 passengers, I had no trouble). The TAT planes are great for photos (at least the one we were on, and other TAT planes looked similar).  TAT planes have the windows bubbled outward a few inches so you can get a good view in multiple directions.  Also, the wings were above the fuselage so the wings did not obstruct viewing much.  In contrast, I also did a summit tour with Talkeetna Aero and the plane was not great for flight seeing since the wings were below the fuselage plus the engine cowling block a lot of the view.  In addition the Talkeetna Aero windows were flat and not as clear/new (adequate, but inferior to TAT's plane)  On Talkeetna Aero,  the pilot had to bank the wing down our your side to get photos (which they did).  But on TAT, I could get great photos anytime (which I did - too many).  If you have never done a Mckinley flight seeing tour before, you will probably enjoy any off them.  But for best experience I would recommend TAT.

Review Text: First of all, in prearranging this trip I was so happy with the friendliness of the staff. The day of our scheduled tour, May 30, 2012,  the weather turned a bit cloudy as it got close to our flight time and the visibility was a concern.  We tried to communicate early with the staff about our concerns of possibly not being able to do our glacier landing or seeing Mt. McKinley because of clouds.  They understood completely and were willing to do whatever was in their realm of control to try to make our experience a good one.  They don't sugar coat things only to have you disappointed.  We got the report from them as to what they expected our flight to be like and they allowed us to make whatever decision we were comfortable with.  We talked with them and they arranged for a later flight time with the idea of reevaluating at that time.  They told us that the weather can dramatically change either way in a short time.  We left but returned shortly thinking we better just cancel because we didn't want to risk not getting out of the experience the things that were important to us.  They pleasantly refunded our money without hesitation. We hung around town just a bit and noticed the weather seemed different so we went back to the office and inquired what they thought and yes, it was just like they said..dramatic change.  So up we went and it was AMAZING!!!!  Visibility was great and we did the glacier landing which is a MUST if you go!!!  What a spectacular view that allows you to experience the immensity of the mountains all around you.  It's a trip that you just have to experience to appreciate it and you will be so glad you did it.  They equip you with boots that fit over your shoes for the glacier landing so don't worry about that.  Just wear a good coat, hat, gloves and sunglasses for optimum comfort.  Take your camer and make a short video if you can so you can relive the moment and share with others.  Our pilot was very nice and shared information as we flew and took questions.  I get motion sickness easily so I took Bonine and also had a patch behind my ear but I will say that I felt the flight was smooth except when you get close to landing and there is some bumping around.  I wasn't sick and never afraid but if you have motion sickness just prepare yourself as I did and you won't have an issue.  This is a super nice company with a great customer satisfaction and I reallly like how they operate.  I highly recommend them.  My only sad point is that we didn't have an extra day in Talkeetna just to hang around and enjoy the cool feeling in that town.  By the way, my husband and I had the privilege of making this trip with our 3 grown children and what a joy to experience this beauty as a family experience we will never forget!!! Thank you Talkeetna Air Taxi!!!

Review Text:
As part of our planned drive from Anchorage to Denali Park, my 13 year old son and I decided to schedule a flight-seeing tour of Denali National Park and Mt. McKinley with Talkeetna Air Taxi based in Talkeetna, AK. The tour turned out to be everything we had hoped for.

First - let's talk pricing. Clearly this is not an inexpensive attraction -- it has to be planned and budgeted for, because, for all the obvious reasons, taking a two hour flight around Mt. McKinley, including a landing on a glacier, is not an inexpensive proposition. Having said this, we believe it was clearly worth the cost, and we believe we received good value in return. Additionally, we asked ourselves the following -- when again will we return to Alaska, and when again will we ever get a chance to see Mt. McKinley this close and from this perspective?

Second - we got extremely lucky with the weather the day we took the tour -- the weather was warm, sunny, and the mountain views were crystal clear -- a picture-perfect day for a flight all around Mt. McKinley and Denali National Park, and landing on a real glacier. This allowed wonderful photography, and even now, reviewing my pictures, it doesn't look like they were taken through a plane window.

For my 13 year old son, landing on the glacier and playing in the snow had to be the highlight of the vacation for him -- he's still talking about all the cool parts of flying around the mountain, seeing the park from the air, and the glacier landing.

Our Talkeetna Air Taxi pilot (Richard, I believe) was extremely knowledgeable, professional, and gracious -- he answered all our questions and really helped make the experience a real enjoyable adventure for us and all the other passengers on the plane. Plus, we had about 40 minutes on the glacier, and that also made it a real grand time, playing in the snow, taking pictures, etc.

I would strongly advise anyone visiting the Anchorage / Denali National Park area to definitely include Talkeetna Air Taxi in their plans. Again, flight-seeing is a bit more expensive than the usual attractions, but it's a once-in-a-lifetime experience that can't be beat. And the folks at TNT really made the experience easy and enjoyable.

One other thing -- the staff at TNT worked with us to reschedule our flight time because we were running a bit late, and, additionally, TNT told me in advance that if the weather were a bit iffy (which it was not, as I mentioned earlier), we could cancel our reservations with no charge at all. This policy is just "good business", and it helped us to decide to go flight-seeing and use TNT.

Review Title: TAT has left its permanent ink on my soul
Review Text: TAT made our 1-hour flight circumnavigating Mt. McKinley so awe-inspiring that there's no way I'm NOT going to do it again.  Literally and non-hyperbolically one of the most amazing experiences of my life.  Our pilot, Will, landed on a snow-packed glacier with no discernible markings indicating length, depth or pitch.  It was so smooth, we didn't even know we'd landed.  Every staff member we encountered was a standard bearer of professionalism.  I am by no means wealthy enough to frivolously spend money on vacations, but this was one of the best $280 I ever spent.  Ever.  If you take the first flight of the morning, you get a free glacier landing.  Maybe this kind of service is common in Alaska, but I can't imagine anyone doing it better.  Highest rating.  5 stars.  Do this.  Before the glaciers are gone.  And before TAT raises their prices when they realize how awesome they are.

Review Text:
Our flight last month (August 11) with Talkeetna Air Taxi was spectacular.

Starting with our making the reservation back in March, their friendly service made everything easy. We really appreciated that they worked with our schedule to meet us when our train arrived and scheduled our flight shortly thereafter (the competitors I contacted didn't offer that flexibility). After discussing the various options with T.A.T. staff, we chose the McKinley Base Camp flight with a glacier landing (1 3/4 hours). By booking early we had already saved $50 per person and since our flight was after 4 PM, they accepted a Northern Lights discount coupon which dropped the price for our group of 4 by 25%.

The flight was smooth and the weather was perfect!!!! Brad, our pilot, was very knowledgeable about Denali and all the nearby mountains and glaciers, was able to answer all of our questions, and altered the route slightly from time to time to assist our picture taking. Our views of Denali, Mt. Foraker, Mt. Hunter, other nearby peaks and numerous glaciers were magnificent and our landing on one of the glaciers was awesome! If you are going to take the flight, make sure you add the glacier landing.

I can't recommend Talkeetna Air Taxi highly enough for a wonderful flightseeing experience.

Review Title: One of the best parts of our trip

This was kinda pricey - but don't miss it. Hint: There is no copilot. That right-hand seat is fair game. TAKE IT!!!

Review Text: This was really tricking in planing, as we arrived in Talkeetna early in the evening and we were scheduled to fly the next morning. But the weather had been forecast as being iffy for next morning. So we called TAT and they explained that if we could be there by 6:30 in the evening we could make a decision to fly or not that night, since the weather is constantly changing in the mountain range. We decided to go that night, looking out at Mount McKinley top one third was in the clouds, the rest of the mountain as well as the rest of the range was partially covered in clouds coming and going. We were suppose to do the grand tour which includes flying the backside of McKinley and a glacier landing at Base Camp.  I asked if it was possible to ride in the co-pilot seat of the air plane and  the service person said she would ask the pilot. As we boarded the plane I was able to fly in the co-pilot seat which gave me the best views for taking pictures.  As we flew out to the range we went though some rain shower in which, if you ever seen a rainbow from a plane it is a circle that goes around the plane, I got some really good pictures.  As flew closer to different mountains in the range I got more great pictures, as the sun was starting to hang low in the horizon. We couldn't fly around the backside of McKinley due to the low cloud cover, but we did land on the glacier which was really cool, it had snowed about 3 feet of snow a few days ago, as we walked on the glacier we would sink to up to over our knees in the soft snow. We stayed on the glacier for about 30 minutes before taking off and heading back to airport.  We were given a discount when we went to pay for the ride, since we didn't do the whole tour. Folks working there are very considerate and I didn't feel at all that they took any advantage of us. Customer service was top notch.

Review Text: I highly recommend doing a flightseeing trip out of Talkeetna, and definitely include a glacier landing.  We had opted to do this, instead of making the trip to Denali, and we were glad we did.  The only thing I would suggest is...if you have a reservation, say later in the day, if the weather is clear in the morning, and you don't have other firm plans, call their office and see if you can get on a flight ASAP.  We were under the impression our 6pm reservation time was firm.  The day was beautiful in the morning and 1st half of the afternoon, but then clouded up and started raining.  We had stopped to talk to one of their reps. in town who was selling flights, and expressed our concern about the weather changing later in the day, but he made no suggestion of going earlier.  The office seemed surprised by this when we checked in.  They did try to call us 2 hours before our scheduled flight, but as with most folks visiting, cell phone service is very spotty up there.  We didn't get the message until it was too late.  We were really disappointed that we were only able to do the shortest flight, and were not able to do the glacier landing.  It still was a great experience, but just keep in mind....call them, and GO when the weather is clear, as it can change very quickly!  Their schedules and reservations definitely seemed flexible to accomodate this.   Maybe not any day, but it was a weekday, and just two of us flying.   Ditto, for asking for deals.  We could have gotten the same deal that day, as I got when I booked months in advance.

Review Text: Please- do yourself a favor and do not book with TAT.  Earlier this month  I had a 7pm flight booked with TAT which was supposed to land on a glacier and return in time to make the last shuttle to the Princess Lodge.  I was assured that there would be no problem on timing since it was important to make this shuttle.  I showed up at about 6pm and checked in.  I waited while several other flights left and was continually assured that everything was fine.  At 7pm no plane for our flight had arrived at the airport.  Again, “everything was OK.” At about 7:30 pm, I overheard the clerk tell someone on the phone “he’s not going to make it, I guess I’ll give a tee shirt and send him on his way.”  It did not take long for me to find out she was talking about me.  The plane had still not arrived and after waiting for almost two hours, I had to walk back to town to catch the shuttle.  No tee shirt was offered, nor would I have accepted it.  I want nothing that would remind me of this disaster.  It was my last night in Talkeetna and I missed what would have been one of the highlights of my visit to Alaska.  I do not know when the plane arrived or any reason for its delay.  Again, book your flight with a more reliable firm such as K2 and avoid my experience.

The first member of staff we met happened to drop into the hotel we were staying in and the reception staff mentioned to her we wanted a trip and she asked if she could  book it for us “or please use my cellphone to book it”, very helpful.  All staff we came across at the office were very nice and friendly. They had to postpone the first trip due to heavy cloud but rebooked for the following afternoon and they said to call in the morning in case they could fit us in earlier if we preferred.   We even got a call from the office asking us if we needed someone to pick us up from our hotel to take us to the airstrip, very efficient. When entering the mountains, he pointed out the names of most of the mountains and glaciers and was more than willing to answer any questions. The scenery was absolutely breathtaking. It was as if God said, "Check this out" when making these mountains. Then we landed on a glacier around 5500 feet in elevation. The view was incredible. The whole time we felt completely safe and comfortable. Like I said, I think this was the crown jewel of our vacation.

Tips: Be sure to wear sunglasses and a light jacket for the glacier. You also have to wear silly booty things over your shoes if you're walking on a glacier. If it's cloudy, take heart! The airport was cloudy but the mountains were not the day we went.

Bottom line: Would I go again? The price was steep but this is definitely a once in a life time. I'll probably never see anything like it again. I would go again if I could afford it.

During the two hour flight and landing, we took over 300 magnificent pictures.  What a way to expereince the majesty of Alaska- a must!

Review Text: I was recently up in Alaska for a wedding in Anchorage. We stayed in Palmer about 1 1/2 hours away from Talkeetna. My wife and I had some reservations driving up to Talkeetna because of busy long weekend.  Taking this trip was so worth it. The views were spectacular. The glacier landing is a must. Review Title: THE highlight of our Alaska vacation!
Review Text: We booked the glacier landing which was incredible.  After flying up towards Mt. McKinley, the pilot did a great job of maneuvering so that people on both sides of the plane could take great photos.  We went places I thought we'd never go in a plane -- between the mountains and circling to land on Ruth Glacier.  With the engine shut down, what a superb site and the silence was stunning.  The pilot was excellent at briefly explaining the sites and the "push to talk" feature allowed the passengers to ask questions during the flight.  This trip is an absolute must!

Review Text:
We have done a lot of sightseeing flights around the World, but this has got to be the best ever. It was a small plane - only 4 seats, and it was quite tight. On the back seat you have to sit crosslegged - but then you have a view to both sides.

The flight took us very low over the mountains around Mount McKinley. The pilot - a young lady - was very informative, sweet and a lot of fun!

We included a glacier landing for an extra price, and that was money very very well spent! It was a fantastic experience landing amidst the mountains and walking out on the glacier. We were, however, also very lucky with the weather.

Review Title: Don't leave Denali without doing this!
Review Text:
We visited Alaska and Denali in Aug 2008.
We hadn't planned to take the air taxi, but made a last minute reservation (just 2 days in advance) when we realized what we might be missing. We were a little apprehensive of going in a little plane, but it was very exciting and probably our best experience in Alaska.
It was just my wife, me, and the pilot (Bob) on the little plane - Bob was very knowledgeable and explained everything there is to know about the rivers, glaciers, moraines, and the mountains. We wree lucky to have clear weather. We flew past the peaks and landed on the little Pica glacier - we spent almost 20 minutes on the glacier, and there are no words to explain how we felt about it.

The flight itself was smooth and we took plenty of pictures. Hats off to Bob and Talkeetna Air Taxi for a great experience!

Review Text: Probably one of the most spectacular things I have ever seen, our flightseeing tour of Denali (Mt Mckinley) in Alaska on Talkeetna Air Taxi was an unforgettable experience. We got the best deal of any of the many local flyers, our pilot Paul was great and everyone was so friendly. We felt safe and reasonably warm for our December flight around the summit. I researched all of the Air Taxis from Anchorage to Talkeetna and chose Talkeetna Air after talking with the locals and they did not disappoint. I highly recommend them to anyone looking for an unforgettable experience.

Review Title: A once in a lifetime experience...dont miss this!
Review Text:
We had booked our reservation months in advance for a Mt. McKinley (Denali) flightseeing tour with glacier landing. Unfortunately, the day before our tour we realized that the weather predictions for the following day were not going to be condusive to seeing "the high one". Review Title: Talkeetna Air Taxi and K2 Aviation
Review Text:
Both K2 and Talkeetna Air Taxi (TAT) get my highest recommendation. Follow along with the bouncing ball, kids, as our tale unfolds:

Pre-booked directly with TAT about a month before leaving for Alaska. Our tour train arrived in Talkeetna about noon and we were scheduled to fly with them at 3pm. Walked over to their shop in town at about 1pm and spoke with Chris, who explained that the weather on the mountain was less than optimum for flightseeing so far that day, and showed us a current computer graphic of the weather system to illustrate the point. We explained that we had only that afternoon available since we were scheduled to leave Talkeetna 11am the following morning. Chris suggested that we kill a few hours in town, cross our fingers, and pray that the weather gods cleared things up enough by early evening to give it a shot. Touched base with him on the hour until 6pm, but the mountain remained fogged in. Sensing our desperation to go up anyway, Chris explained that he'd be happy to fly us around the lower part of the Ruth Glacier on a less extensive tour, but strongly urged us to call it a day since we were likely to be unhappy with the view. Look. When a pilot tells you to cancel...you cancel. We told Chris we'd try him again early the next morning if the weather cleared, and TAT refunded our deposit no questions asked. I have to commend Chris and TAT for their helpfulness and honesty.

Fast forward to the following morning. We take a look out the back deck of the Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge at 7:45am. The sky is clear and the mountains are in plain view. I call TAT back, but their entire morning schedule is committed to taking up climbers that they were unable to get up the day before, and they can't possibly get us up and back before we have to leave. TAT made their bones depositing climbers on Denali, and understandably they're priority #1. We're out of luck and about out of time.

It's a horrible sight to see a grown man cry. It really is. In a last dicth effort at salvaging the most anticipated part of our trip, I run over to the concierge desk at the lodge and BEG the woman to put us on something...anything...a hot air baloon if necessary... some Wright Brothers pedal-powered contraption...that can get us up to Denali and back by 11am.

Angels exist. Trust me. I found one. Within 10 minutes, the concierge (who is now a viable candidate for sainthood if she performs just TWO more miracles) called us and set to get ready...she got seats for 4 of us with K2 Aviation at 8:30, and we'd be back in time to make our bus. Take note, my countrymen. I do solemnly swear that I shall willingly fall upon my sword for this woman should the need ever arise.

Mike at K2 took us up in a 5-seat Cessna for the ride of our lives on their Denali Grand Tour. Nothing compares with the sight of seeing the biggest rock on the North American continent up close and personal. Loss for words. Fill in your favorite superlatives. There's a dreamlike quality to the entire landscape, as if it were some massive painted backdrop for a Cecil B. DeMille film. Mike gave us the 4-1-1 on the geologic environs as we flew around Denali, Foraker, Hunter, the Ruth Glacier and the Talkeetna Mountain range. Absolutely the highlight of our trip to Alaska. It'll be yours, too.

The flyguys of Talkeetna are a cooperative and close-knit band of brothers who are constantly in radio contact with each other about flying conditions in the area. You won't find a friendlier, more informative bunch of "Right Stuff"-ers anywhere this side of NASA. Hats off, and sincere thanks to the crews at both K2 AND TAT.

And, of course, to my guardan angel at the Talkeetna Alaskan concierge desk. Who loves ya, baby?

Strongly suggest that you make arrangements well before you leave for Alaska if you're planning on going on a Denali flight. Space fills up quick (and we got damn lucky). And be prepared on any given day for the mountain to do what the mountain is wont to do. Anything big enough to create its own weather system ain't arranging its day around YOUR schedule. Denali is like a box of chocolates, Forrest...

.

Review Title: Talkeetna Air Taxi - GOTTA DO IT!
Review Text: Our top priority in Talkeetna was flightseeing over Mt. McKinley (Denali). We booked with Talkeetna Air Taxi for the Grand Denali tour with Glacier Landing. We had 2 Toursaver books so my family of 4 saved $440. It was cloudy (as usual) so we were thinking that our trip might be a bummer, but boy were we wrong! We had the time of our lives! My hat's off to those pilots, they really know their stuff! The pilot did a great job of stay below the clouds so that we could see the sharp cliffs and massive glaciers. Many times we were so close that the proximity warning would enunciate "500" warning us that we were within 500 feet of the terrain. But I never felt scared. My 12-year old daughter was petrified to board the plane, but soon she began to enjoy herself and now she'll tell you that flightseeing was one of her favorite activities in Alaska. Our glacier landing was as smooth as silk. What an awesome feeling to stand in such a majestic place! After we took-off again, the pilot found a hole in the clouds and after a steep assent we popped out above the clouds for a perfectly clear view of Denali's summit. WOW! If you have any chance to take this trip - DO IT!
